BUILT THE RUNWAY . 
READY FOR TAKE-OFF .
Engineering the Foundation for  
High-Velocity Growth
Fiscal 2026 was the pivotal year in which AXISCADES completed 
its structural re-architecture, transitioning from a service-led 
“Architect” to a product-led “Constructor”. By divesting legacy, 
services-based businesses, we unlocked the strategic fuel 
required to fund our long-term roadmap and secure high-margin 
product ownership. Simultaneously, the build-out of shared tri-use 
infrastructure provided the physical foundation needed to scale 
our active pipeline of mission-critical systems across aerospace, 
defence, ESAI and, now, space..
This evolution is validated by the outperformance of our specialised 
growth platforms and a record improvement in operational 
productivity, as we made a solid beginning in decoupling our 
top-line potential from headcount expansion. We have finalised 
the ‘structural engineering’ of our foundation; we ‘built the runway’ 
in FY2026, and we’re ‘gearing for take-off’ in FY2027. With our 
core platforms firmly anchored, AXISCADES is now cleared for 
departure and positioned to convert this runway into visible, non-
linear momentum.

THE BIG PICTURE
A runway built for 
focused growth
FY2026 combined stronger operating performance with the capabilities, 
leadership and choices required for a more focused AXISCADES.
The year in context
Revenue and EBITDA increased in FY2026, with EBITDA growing faster than revenue and 
the margin expanding. This operating progress was achieved while the Group invested 
in facilities, programmes, leadership and execution systems. The result was a stronger 
base, and also a clear agenda: convert programmes into delivery and cash, commission 
capacity against qualified demand and keep capital linked to customer-backed milestones. 
The runway has been built on domain depth, customer relationships, technical talent, 
manufacturing infrastructure and a more disciplined model for allocating capital.
A clearer perimeter after year-end
During the first quarter of FY2027, AXISCADES announced the Engineering Services 
Divestment Programme and formalised four growth Platforms: Aerospace Manufacturing, 
SCM & MRO; Defence Solutions; XiDA Inc, the AI-centric ESAI platform; and the Space 
Division. These are post-balance-sheet developments. They do not alter the reported 
FY2026 results; they explain the direction in which the FY2026 foundations are intended to 
be deployed.
The pages that follow separate reported outcomes from later strategic actions. They 
describe what AXISCADES is, what changed during the year, how the business creates 
value and which execution disciplines will determine the next phase.
What FY2026 put in place
The first foundation was a more deliberate portfolio logic. AXISCADES continued to serve a 
broad FY2026 reporting perimeter, but management increasingly directed attention towards 
the areas where domain knowledge, regulated-customer access and physical realisation 
can reinforce one another. Aerospace, Defence and ESAI formed the operating centre of 
that logic. The later four-Platform structure made the direction more explicit.
The second foundation was capability. Engineering remained the starting point, but not 
the intended end point. The Company advanced facilities, electronics, test, manufacturing 
engineering, supply-chain capability and programme leadership so that it can assume 
responsibility across more of the customer lifecycle. This matters because qualification, 
configuration control and reliable physical delivery are the gates through which engineering 
knowledge becomes a more durable commercial position.The third foundation was institutional. 
FY2026 brought a stronger focus on 
programme accountability, financial 
control, leadership depth and common 
management systems. These 
disciplines, while less visible than a 
facility or a product, determine whether 
a larger business remains governable. 
As the Group adds manufacturing, 
selective acquisitions and more 
complex international structures, the 
quality of these controls becomes an 
important part of the investment case.
AXISCADES entered FY2026 with established engineering credentials 
and ended it with a clearer basis for scale. The year strengthened the 
financial and operating foundations of the business while management 
advanced its move towards product-led, manufacturing-led and 
intellectual-property-led growth across Aerospace, Defence, ESAI, and 
in the future, Space.12.4 %

AXISCADES AT A GLANCE
Engineering depth,  
increasingly built into products
AXISCADES combines domain engineering, strategic electronics and manufacturing capability 
for global and national programmes.
AXISCADES Technologies Limited is a Bengaluru-headquartered 
technology and engineering company serving Aerospace, Defence, 
electronics, semiconductor and AI applications. The Group works 
across the product lifecycle, from design and analysis to manufacturing, 
system integration, supply-chain support, testing and sustainment.
What we do
AXISCADES addresses programmes where engineering precision, 
configuration control, certification and delivery discipline matter. Its 
capabilities cover mechanical and electrical design, embedded electronics, 
test systems, tooling, wire harnesses, precision assemblies, system 
integration and technical lifecycle support. This combination allows the 
Company to participate at multiple points in a customer’s product and 
programme lifecycle.The operating model is built around 
long-duration relationships with original 
equipment manufacturers, Tier-1 suppliers, 
national agencies and technology 
companies. Customer proximity is 
supported by delivery and business teams 
in India, North America and Europe.

AXISCADES AT A GLANCE

Where AXISCADES sits in the value chain
AXISCADES sits between the origin of a complex engineering 
requirement and the accepted product or system that must 
perform in service. At one end of the chain, the work may involve 
architecture, analysis, mechanical or electrical design, embedded 
development and product data. At the other, it may involve tooling, 
sourcing, electronics, harnesses, assemblies, integration, test and 
lifecycle support. The strategic opportunity lies in connecting these 
activities under clearer programme ownership.
Our business model is anchored in a high-fidelity, IP-driven 
architecture designed for non-linear scalability and premium 
value capture across the deep-tech landscape. The Company 
participates principally in low- and medium-volume, high-
complexity contexts where a small number of technically 
demanding deliverables can carry significant programme 
consequence. Entry is governed by customer approval, 
certification, security, quality and performance history. Once 
established, these same requirements can support longer 
relationships and recurring participation.
Why the combination matters
Engineering provides insight into how the product should work. 
Electronics and embedded capability allow that insight to be 
carried into the product. Manufacturing and supply-chain capability 
make the design repeatable. Testing, configuration and lifecycle 
support preserve performance after delivery. The combination 
reduces the number of external hand-offs that a customer must 
manage and allows AXISCADES to retain learning across stages.
For investors, the significance is economic as well as technical. 
A broader span of controlled responsibility can support higher-
value participation, deeper customer relevance and more reusable 
knowledge. It can also increase capital intensity, working-capital 
exposure and execution risk. The Company looks to expand 
responsibility only where the commercial model, customer evidence 
and operating controls are sufficiently mature.

FY2026 PERFORMANCE SNAPSHOT
Growth strengthened;  
focus on conversion 
Higher revenue, faster EBITDA growth and a wider margin demonstrated operating progress in FY2026.Operating performance
Revenue from operations grew by 12.4% over FY2025. EBITDA 
grew by 24.6%, close to twice the pace of revenue growth, and 
the margin expanded by 150 basis points. Profit before tax, before 
exceptional items, increased by 36.5% to `124.76 crore. The year 
included a net exceptional charge of `11.17 crore, after which 
reported profit before tax was `113.59 crore.
The improvement reflects a more favourable domain mix, delivery 
discipline and productivity. Revenue per employee rose to `39.94 
lakh and EBITDA per employee increased to `6.12 lakh. Employee 
benefit expense as a share of revenue declined, supporting 
operating leverage.
Balance Sheet and Cash: Funding the 
Infrastructure of AXISCADES 3.0
Strategic investments drove consolidated capital expenditure to 
`134.44 crore during the fiscal year as the Group aggressively 
built out manufacturing infrastructure, advanced testing facilities, 
and specialised programme capabilities. To support this scaling 
operational footprint, trade receivables rose to `411.34 crore and 
inventory levels reached `78.97 crore, reflecting the high-intensity 
nature of our current delivery and acceptance cycles. Operating 
cash flow recorded a transitional outflow of `1.36 crore as we 
deployed liquidity into long-cycle assets, leading net debt to reach 
`230.98 Crore to anchor our infrastructure expansion.
These foundational financial movements represent a rigorous 
financial framework for our next stage of evolution. Execution in 
Fiscal 2027 is focusing on the disciplined conversion of deliverables 
into formal customer acceptance and cash receipts, ensuring every 
new capital commitment is strictly anchored to qualified market 
demand and the attainment of visible programme milestones.
The quality of the earnings movement
The central operating signal was the difference between the pace 
of revenue growth and EBITDA growth. Faster EBITDA growth 
indicates that mix, delivery productivity and cost absorption moved 
in the right direction during the year. The increase in profit before 
exceptional items provides a second view of that improvement 
because it separates the underlying operating result from charges 
and gains that do not represent the recurring run rate.
Reported profit after tax moved differently because the year carried 
a higher tax charge and net exceptional cost. The distinction 
matters. To provide a clear and balanced view of performance, 
the report presents statutory measures as the primary basis of 
reporting, complemented, where relevant, by clearly defined and 
reconciled management measures that offer additional insight into 
the Company’s underlying operating strength.
An investment year with a cash consequence
The increase in capital expenditure reflects the decision to build 
capability ahead of the next production and qualification cycle. 
In Aerospace and Defence, this sequence is often unavoidable: customers expect evidence of equipment, 
process, people and control before they 
commit larger programmes. It nevertheless 
creates a timing gap between cash 
deployed and returns realised. The value 
of FY2026 investment will therefore be 
demonstrated through commissioning, 
customer qualification, utilisation, yield and 
cash generation in subsequent periods.
Working capital carried a similar timing 
issue. Receivables and inventory support 
programme delivery, but they also absorb 
liquidity and can obscure the quality of 
reported growth if acceptance or collection 
is delayed. Management’s FY2027 priority 
is to bring commercial scope, long-lead 
sourcing, customer inspection, invoicing 
and collection into a more synchronised 
operating rhythm.

ABOUT THE COMPANY
Built around complex products 
and long programmes 
AXISCADES works where engineering knowledge leads to qualification, industrialisation, delivery and 
years of lifecycle support.
AXISCADES works where a requirement has to survive design reviews, 
qualification, customer audits and first-article evidence before it becomes 
a product. That sequence is slow, but it is also the barrier to entry. 
Our offer is built to carry more of it, from system engineering through 
electronics, tooling and precision manufacturing to lifecycle support.
A connected offer
The Company’s offer starts with product and system 
engineering. Teams work on mechanical and electrical 
design, analysis, embedded systems, technical 
publications and product-lifecycle support. The 
offer extends into strategic electronics, automatic 
test equipment, hardware realisation, tooling, wire 
harnesses, precision manufacturing, integration and 
supply-chain management.
This connected offer matters because value in 
regulated industries is created across gates. A 
sound design must be qualified. A qualified design 
must be industrialised. Industrial output must meet 
configuration, quality and acceptance requirements. 
The supplier that can manage more of these hand-offs 
can take greater programme responsibility and build 
more durable customer relationships.
Delivery model
During FY2026, 76% of revenue was delivered offshore 
and 24% onsite. Time-and-material engagements 
represented 71% of revenue and fixed-price 
engagements 29%. These measures describe the 
reported delivery mix; the strategic direction is to 
increase scalable, product-led and manufacturing-led 
value without compromising engineering depth.
AXISCADES supports customers through delivery 
centres, offices and subsidiaries in India and 
international markets. The Company operates three 
offices in India and 13 international offices across seven 
countries. Group and standalone footprint measures 
are therefore kept distinct.

Customers and markets
Customers include global original equipment manufacturers, Tier-1 suppliers, national defence and research 
organisations, military end users and technology companies. Work is performed under customer confidentiality 
and export-control requirements. For that reason, this report describes capabilities and programme classes without 
disclosing restricted customer or programme information.
Why mission-critical work behaves differently
Aerospace, Defence and advanced electronics do not move directly from idea to volume. Programmes advance 
through design reviews, qualification, customer audits, security requirements, first-article evidence, configuration 
approval and final acceptance. A technically sound solution can therefore remain commercially immature until the 
complete evidence chain is in place. AXISCADES’ operating model is built to manage these gates across long  
programme cycles.
From specialist supplier to programme 
participant
The Company participates at a single stage or across several 
stages. A specialist engagement may begin with design, analysis or 
a test requirement. Greater responsibility may add industrialisation, 
sourcing, build, integration and sustainment. Each additional stage 
creates potential value, but also transfers schedule, capital and 
performance risk to AXISCADES. The decision to move further is 
therefore based on customer relevance, control of the interfaces 
and the return available after risk.
Long-duration participation creates a learning advantage. Product 
data, process knowledge, supplier experience and field feedback 
can improve the next delivery and shorten the next development 
cycle. Where rights permit, this learning can be converted into 
reference architectures, qualified methods and reusable assets. 
Where customer ownership or confidentiality applies, it remains 
segregated and protected.
A globally connected, India-centred model
International teams provide customer proximity, local commercial 
understanding and access to technology ecosystems. India 
provides the principal base for engineering, electronics and the 
manufacturing capacity being developed. The model creates 
value only when the connection is operational: customer insight 
The cost of failure is also different. A late or non-conforming part can interrupt a customer’s wider programme. 
A data or security breach can damage access to sensitive work. An undocumented change can compromise 
traceability. This makes process discipline, controlled information, supplier quality and honest escalation as 
important as the original engineering solution.

What makes the model resilient
Resilience comes from domain 
diversification, reusable capability, long 
customer relationships and the ability to 
serve more than one lifecycle stage. It 
also depends on a disciplined response 
to concentration, long-lead supply, 
working capital, export controls, cyber risk 
and critical talent. The Company seeks 
to deepen its position without allowing 
breadth to weaken programme ownership.ABOUT THE COMPANY

VISION, MISSION AND STRATEGIC AMBITION
Ambition,  translated into 
operating choices
The destination is product-led and non-linear growth; the route is governed investment, programme 
conversion and stronger execution.
AXISCADES’ vision and mission set a clear direction: use established 
domain knowledge to become more product-led, more technology-led 
and less dependent on linear expansion. Power 930 gives us a long-
term FY2030 horizon.
Power 930: the strategic ambition
Power 930 expresses management’s long-term ambition for 
the scale and earnings quality of AXISCADES by FY2030. The 
report deliberately does not present that ambition as a straight-
line forecast. Aerospace and Defence programmes have long 
qualification and delivery cycles; capacity must be commissioned 
in stages; acquisitions and partnerships require integration; and 
reported outcomes depend on acceptance, collections and the 
timing of customer decisions. The FY2026 theme “Built the Runway. 
Ready for Take-off.” describes a year of foundations. AXISCADES 
invested in leadership, technology, facilities and programme 
positions while improving operating performance.
Transformation in progress
The vision defines the kind of enterprise AXISCADES intends to 
become: product-driven, technology-led and capable of non-
linear value creation. The mission defines the means: deepen core 
capability, use partnerships selectively and invest with discipline. 
Together they require management to make choices about what the 
Company will own, what it will partner for and what it will decline.
A long-term ambition such as “Power 930” directs attention towards 
addressable markets, business mix, operating margins, capital 
needs and the organisational capacity required by FY2030. It also 
makes the dependencies visible: programme conversion, qualified 
capacity, supply-chain readiness, acquisition integration, working-
capital release and stronger returns.
To be a product-driven, non-linear technology leader in 
Aerospace, Defence and ESAI, delivering cutting-edge

behind the ambition
For customers, the ambition means greater 
responsibility, more indigenous capability 
and dependable lifecycle support. For 
employees, it creates deeper technical 
paths, product ownership and new 
manufacturing careers. For partners and 
suppliers, it creates clearer programmes 
and opportunities to build capability. For 
the nation, it supports strategic technology 
and localisation. For investors, it should 
translate into growth, cash, resilience and 
returns.
These outcomes are connected. 
Customer trust supports programme 
continuity. Skills and supplier depth support 
quality. Quality and acceptance support 
cash conversion. Cash and returns provide 
the capacity to reinvest. The strategic 
ambition becomes durable only when this 
stakeholder compact remains balanced.

INVESTMENT CASE
From architect to constructor:  
capturing non-linear value.
AXISCADES combines attractive domain demand with engineering depth, strategic infrastructure and a 
clearer model for capital deployment.
The investment case rests on a practical proposition. 
AXISCADES already participates in long-cycle Aerospace, 
Defence and advanced-electronics markets; it has demonstrated 
operating leverage; and it is building the capability to carry more 
value from design into products, systems and lifecycle support. 
1. Exposure to structurally 
supported domains
Global aerospace demand is anchored by 
an unprecedented aircraft order backlog 
exceeding 17,000 units and nearly twelve 
years of current production capacity, as 
major airframers designate India as a 
primary destination for diversified Tier-1 
sourcing and supply-chain resilience. 
Domestic Defence growth is fundamentally 
driven by India’s `6.81 lakh crore budget 
and an uncompromising national 
commitment to Atmanirbhar Bharat, 
where our high-velocity portfolio of active 
design wins position us to take full-cycle 
responsibility for prestigious national 
3. Evidence of structural shift toward high-margin 
verticals
In FY2026, EBITDA grew faster than revenue and the EBITDA margin 
expanded. The primary driver of margin accretion was the high-
velocity performance of the Defence vertical. While total revenue 
grew by double digits, the Defence segment’s revenue increased 
by 24.7% (to `377.70 crore), while its segment profit grew by an 
extraordinary 91% YoY. By concentrating resources on indigenous 
defence programs and mission-critical “Systems & Solutions”, the 
Group replaced legacy low-margin work with high-value contracts 
that carry structurally superior margins and longer lifecycles.
4. Shared Manufacturing Infrastructure: Driving 
Value-Chain Migration
AXISCADES is fundamentally pivoting from a service-led 
“architect” of designs to a product-led “constructor” of mission-
ready assemblies, a transformation designed to capture a 
significantly larger share of the programme value chain. This 
migration is powered by our new capability clusters at Devanahalli 
and Hyderabad, where shared precision, test, and assembly 
infrastructure serves electronics, aerospace, defence, and 
emerging space applications. This shared architecture improves 
asset utilisation and shortens programme mobilisation, provided 
capacity expansion is strictly phased against qualified demand and 
visible milestones. By migrating toward mission-ready “Systems & 
Solutions” through this common foundation, we are institutionalising 
a model for non-linear growth that decouples revenue potential 
from headcount. This structural shift ensures our top line scales efficiently without a proportional increase 
in the cost base, anchoring our trajectory 
toward the ambitious revenue and margin 
targets defined in the Power 930 roadmap.
5. Explicit Capital Discipline and 
Performance Conversion
Our investment rationale is anchored in a 
rigorous capital-allocation framework that 
prioritises “execution over announcement,” 
strictly funding programs only against 
customer-backed milestones and qualified 
market demand. Bolstered by proceeds 
from our strategic divestment programme 
spread in multiple phases over 2-3 years, 
AXISCADES will maintain substantial 
liquidity buffers to fully fund the “Power 930” 
roadmap, supported by short to medium 
term bridge borrowings. This discipline

WHY IT MATTERS
Transparent bridges prevent strategic change from obscuring the underlying operating and cash trajectory.
Strategy may change the perimeter. Reporting preserves the evidence line.
Comparability matters most when the business perimeter is changing. 
This three-year view keeps each period in its proper place: FY2025 
established the financial baseline, FY2026 strengthened operating 
performance and capability, and FY2027 begins the transition towards 
a more focused Platform structure.
FY2025 marked the first year in which Group revenue exceeded `1,000 crore and provided 
the base for the next phase. The Annual Report described the Company primarily through 
Aerospace, Defence and ESAI, alongside other engineering services. It also introduced the 
intent to move towards non-linear, product-led growth.FY2025: establish the baseline
FY2026 delivered higher revenue, faster EBITDA growth and margin expansion. The Company 
advanced infrastructure, added leadership capability, increased capital expenditure and 
deepened programme positions. These actions built capacity for future execution while 
increasing the need for tighter working-capital and cash-conversion discipline.
The FY2026 front end applies integrated-reporting discipline by connecting strategy, six 
capitals, stakeholders, material matters, risk and outcomes.FY2026: build the foundations
During the first quarter of FY2027, AXISCADES announced its Engineering Services Divestment 
Programme and set out four growth Platforms. As transactions progress, investors will receive 
a transparent bridge between the FY2026 reported perimeter, continuing operations, disposed 
activities and any management-defined measures.
The FY2027 reporting will therefore be twofold: show progress against the Platform strategy and 
preserve comparability. Transaction proceeds, closing adjustments, contingent consideration 
and new investments will be reported when recognised or firmly committed.FY2027: explain the transition
Why a three-year lens is necessary
A single-year comparison can mislead when the strategic and reporting perimeter is changing. FY2025, 
FY2026 and FY2027 answer different questions. The first shows the scale and structure from which the 
strategy began. The second shows what the existing Group achieved and invested during the reporting 
year. The third will show how transactions, retained businesses and new Platform accountabilities alter 
the continuing enterprise.
The three-year lens also separates strategic causality from accounting timing. Capability built in FY2026 
may support programmes recognised later. A transaction announced in FY2027 may reshape future 
results without changing the FY2026 record. Maintaining this distinction protects both the credibility of 
the theme and the comparability of performance.

Dear Shareholders,
FY2026 will be remembered as the year in which AXISCADES 
converted strategic intent into a more definitive institutional 
direction. We entered the year with a clear conviction: the next 
phase of value creation would not come from preserving every 
activity in the portfolio. It would come from concentrating capital, 
talent and management attention on the businesses where 
AXISCADES can earn enduring relevance, differentiation and scale. 
“Built the Runway. Ready for Take-off.” captures this conviction. 
It reflects a deliberate evolution of the enterprise rather than a 
response to short-term circumstances.
The Company delivered growth while undertaking this change. 
Revenue from operations increased by 12.4% and EBITDA 
increased by 24.6%, with Aerospace, Defence and ESAI together 
contributing approximately 78% of consolidated revenue. These 
outcomes are important, but the deeper significance of FY2026 
lies in what changed beneath the numbers: the quality of the 
portfolio, the build-out of strategic infrastructure, the strengthening 
of customer and partner relationships, and a clearer pathway from 
engineering capability to manufacturing, systems, products and 
intellectual property.
A strategic moment for India and AXISCADES
The industries in which we operate are being reshaped 
simultaneously. Global aerospace supply chains are seeking 
resilience, responsiveness and greater manufacturing depth. 
Defence modernisation is creating sustained demand for 
indigenous systems, strategic electronics and integration capability. 
Space is opening to commercial participation at unprecedented 
speed. Semiconductors, electronics and artificial intelligence are 
converging to redefine products, factories and mission-critical 
systems. India is becoming an increasingly important design, 
engineering and manufacturing partner in each of these domains.AXISCADES enters this period with more 
than 30 years of engineering knowledge, 
trusted relationships with global original 
equipment manufacturers, experience 
in complex defence programmes and 
a growing electronics and artificial 
intelligence platform. Our responsibility is to 
translate those advantages into a business 
model that captures more value across 
the product lifecycle. That means moving 
beyond a predominantly linear services 
construct towards a more scalable mix 
of manufacturing, integrated solutions, 
proprietary products, reusable platforms 
and IP-led offerings.
From capability breadth to 
strategic concentration
This evolution should not be read as a 
rejection of our engineering heritage. 
Engineering remains the foundation of 
AXISCADES. It is the knowledge base that 
allows us to design for manufacturability, 
qualify safety-critical products, understand 
customer platforms and solve problems 
that carry high technical and regulatory 
barriers. Our strategic task is to carry that 
knowledge further downstream - from 
design to build, from analysis to integration, 
and from project delivery to lifecycle 
participation.Our strategic realignment is a surgical reallocation of 
capital and capability, not an exit. We are not narrowing 
our ambition; we are sharpening it. By concentrating the 
enterprise around the mission-critical platforms where 
our engineering pedigree creates the greatest economic 
value, we have definitively migrated from a service-led 
‘Architect’ to a product-led ‘Constructor.’ Having built 
a robust runway in Fiscal 2026, AXISCADES is now 
cleared for takeoff toward our Power 930 vision.

Applying the lessons of the 
fourth quarter
FY2026 did not close exactly as planned. 
Approximately `142 crore of revenue 
could not be recognised before year-end because of supply-chain disruption, input-material availability, 
programme scheduling and transaction-related transition factors. 
The underlying orders remained intact and management views 
the disruption as a one-off timing event. Nevertheless, it exposed 
areas where a manufacturing-led AXISCADES will need to 
strengthen forward controls, and the timing shift affected revenue, 
EBITDA and cash conversion in the fourth quarter.
The principal lesson has been internalised by strengthening 
the identification and stocking of critical long-lead items, 
placing orders earlier, improving supplier tracking and building 
greater resilience into the supply chain. Where technically and 
commercially possible, alternative sourcing and procurement 
buffers will be developed. This may require more selective 
working-capital deployment, but the objective is to protect delivery 
predictability and customer commitments.

schedules, customer acceptance milestones, configuration 
changes and billing readiness. A programme is not complete 
when production ends; it is complete when the product is 
accepted, invoiced and collected. That full order-to-cash view will 
increasingly define our operating cadence.

The transition towards a more integrated operating model also 
requires better systems. During FY2026, the Company initiated 
a CRM programme, acquired licences, began configuration 
and conducted initial user training. This forms the first layer of a 
broader effort to improve pipeline visibility, programme hand-offs 
and management information. The next stage will progressively 
connect commercial commitments with order-to-cash and 
procure-to-pay workflows across procurement, production, 
quality, delivery and cash milestones.In early FY2027, we took the next step towards a unified Defence 
delivery structure across electronics and systems integration, 
supported by dedicated operations leadership and a more focused 
systems mandate. The objective is to create one operating view 
across Defence programmes, with clearer accountability from 
commercial commitment through delivery and cash realisation.
Customer continuity remained a first-order priority as the portfolio 
was reshaped. The businesses being divested and the retained 
growth platforms have largely distinct customer and delivery teams, 
reducing direct execution risk. At the same time, the movement of 
enabling functions and co-located teams requires careful transition 
planning. The retained organisation is therefore strengthening core 
capabilities in operations, quality, programme management, supply 
chain, finance, HR and IT so that customers experience no loss of 
responsiveness or ownership.
Our FY2027 operating priorities
First, convert the deferred and embedded programmes into 
delivery, acceptance, revenue and cash with greater predictability. 
Second, complete the transition of capabilities into DAL and bring 
the first phases of DAC and MAC online against qualified demand 
during FY2027. Third, scale Defence manufacturing and complete-

procurement, production and cash. Fifth, maintain customer and 
employee continuity through the portfolio transition.Our operating measures will increasingly 
reflect these priorities: pipeline depth 
and conversion, on-time programme

and acceptance performance, working-

OEMs, before opportunities convert into

intervene before a programme delay 
becomes a revenue or liquidity issue.
FY2026 built the runway for AXISCADES. 
The facilities, programmes and capabilities

Power 930: a strategic architecture for value

milestones by which progress will be judged.

productisation and deeper participation in customer programmes.

BUSINESS MODEL
Value grows as responsibility 
travels further
AXISCADES connects engineering, qualification, industrialisation, production and lifecycle support 
within long-duration customer programmes.
The business model converts domain knowledge and customer access 
into programme outcomes. AXISCADES applies people, technology, 
facilities and partnerships across a series of controlled gates, earns 
through engineering and product delivery, and reinvests cash and 
learning into reusable capability.Input What it enables
Domain knowledge An understanding of programme, certification, mission and lifecycle requirements
Technical talent Engineering, electronics, software, manufacturing, quality and programme execution
Customer relationships Access to long-cycle opportunities and qualification pathways
Technology and intellectual property Reusable designs, embedded systems, test assets and AI-enabled methods
Facilities and supply chain Industrialisation, production, integration, testing and sustainment
Financial capital and governance Selective investment, risk control and operating resilience
5
principal earning routes
3
gates before scale: qualify,  
accept, collect
6
linked value-creation stages
How we earn
Revenue is earned through engineering engagements, fixed-price deliverables, product and system 
supply, manufacturing and integration, supply-chain support and lifecycle services. Commercial 
structures vary by programme. Cash conversion depends on clear milestones, customer inspection 
and acceptance, timely invoicing and collection.Activities: the six-stage value path
1. Select:  qualify the customer problem, strategic fit, contract route and expected 
return.
2. Engineer:  develop architecture, design, analysis, electronics, software and 
product data.
3. Qualify:  meet technical, regulatory, quality, security and customer-acceptance 
requirements.
4. Industrialise:  define tooling, sourcing, processes, fixtures, test methods and 
production readiness.
5. Build and integrate:  manufacture, assemble, test, configure and deliver  
products or complete systems.
6. Sustain:  support supply chains, upgrades, maintenance, repair, overhaul and 
lifecycle availability.
Not every programme necessarily uses all six stages. The strategic objective is to take 
responsibility for more of the chain where AXISCADES can improve customer  
outcomes and earn an appropriate return.

BUSINESS MODEL  
(contd... )
Outputs and outcomes
Outputs include qualified designs, test 
systems, electronics, harnesses, tools, 
manufactured assemblies, integrated 
solutions and lifecycle support. Customer 
outcomes are improved development 
speed, reliable delivery, localisation, 
availability and reduced programme risk. 
For AXISCADES, the intended outcomes 
are durable relationships, reusable 
capability, higher-value revenue, cash 
generation and returns on invested capital.
How economics change along 
the value path
Each stage has a different economic 
character. Engineering assignments 
are principally knowledge- and talent-
led. Qualification adds specialist 
evidence, customer interaction and 
time. Industrialisation introduces tooling, 
process, supplier and production-
readiness costs. Build and integration 
require inventory, capacity, quality control 
and working capital. Sustainment can 
create longer-duration participation, but 
requires service readiness, product data 
and performance accountability.
The strategic objective is not to move 
every programme to the final stage. It 
is to identify where a greater span of 
responsibility improves the customer 
outcome and the return after capital and 
risk. In some programmes, a high-value 
engineering or test role may be the right 
position. In others, design ownership and 
manufacturing are inseparable. 
The reinvestment loop
Cash generated from engineering, products, manufacturing and lifecycle activity is allocated first to programme 
continuity and financial resilience, then to qualified capacity, technology, people and selective inorganic growth. 
Operating and customer learning influences where that capital goes next. A strong business model therefore closes 
the loop between market choice, programme outcome, cash and reinvestment.The commercial architecture
Commercial terms tend to reflect the risk accepted at each 
gate. Engineering work may be billed through time-and-
material or defined milestones. Product and system work 
requires clarity on specifications, change control, long-
lead material, customer-furnished information, inspection, 
acceptance, warranty and payment triggers. Lifecycle 
arrangements require clear service levels, configuration 
records and responsibility for obsolescence.
This architecture affects cash as much as revenue. A 
programme can appear technically advanced while 
remaining commercially immature if scope, acceptance 
evidence or billing triggers are unresolved. AXISCADES 
therefore brings commercial, engineering, supply, quality 
and finance decisions together earlier in the programme. 
The intended result is less ambiguity at the point of 
delivery and a shorter path from accepted output to 
collection.
Learning as an economic asset
Every completed programme can leave behind more than 
revenue. It can create design rules, test libraries, process 
parameters, qualified supplier knowledge, configuration 
practices and field insight. When ownership and customer 
rights allow, these assets can improve the next bid, 
shorten the next qualification cycle or become part of 
a configurable product or platform. This is the practical 
mechanism behind non-linear growth.
Learning is not automatically reusable. Customer 
information may be restricted, programme data may be 
segregated, and technical know-how may belong wholly 
or partly to another party. The Company endeavours to 
identify its own intellectual capital, protect it contractually, 
control access and distinguish permitted reuse from 
customer-specific knowledge. Governance of the asset is 
therefore part of its economic value.

VALUE CREATION FRAMEWORK
Six capitals, tested through 
outcomes
Value is created when capital inputs reinforce one another and result in customer, 
employee, national and investor outcomes.
AXISCADES uses an integrated value-creation lens to connect strategy 
with resources, relationships and consequences. The framework does 
not treat the six capitals as separate stores of value. It shows how 
financial, manufactured, intellectual, human, social and relationship, 
and natural capital combine within programmes.
AXISCADES 3.0 represents a fundamental structural realignment designed to transition the Group from a  
design-led “architect” of engineering services to a product-led “constructor” of mission-ready systems. Our  
Value Creation Framework is architected to leverage a multi-decadal engineering pedigree to capture non-linear 
value across high-growth, structurally supported domains. By reorganising our resources into distinct strategic  
objectives, we ensure that every capital input is converted into high-fidelity outputs that drive superior  
stakeholder outcomes.
Knowledge Sovereignty: Embedding Global Deep-Tech IP via Mirroring Architecture
Primary Capital: Intellectual
Inputs: Our value creation is anchored by a distinguished engineering legacy and specialised 
proprietary knowledge gained over 15,000 cumulative man-years of domain experience. This 
includes deep technical expertise in mission-critical avionics, radar data processing, and 
electronic warfare subsystems.
Outputs We are converting this legacy into an aggressive migration from providing man-hour intensive 
services to taking full design-to-manufacture responsibility for mission-ready systems. Central 
to this is our “Mirroring Architecture,” which facilitates the seamless transfer and embedding of 
sophisticated international technology and manufacturing IP into our domestic clusters.
Outcomes The ultimate result is the establishment of a formidable technical moat and an IP-led growth 
engine. By institutionalising a “Constructor” mandate, the Group captures expansive value 
across the entire product lifecycle, ensuring that AXISCADES moves from being a service 
provider to a primary owner of mission-critical outcomes.The Talent Runway: Institutionalising the “Constructor” Mandate for  
Non-Linear Scale
Primary Capital: Human
Inputs: Our framework relies on a stable, high-fidelity workforce of 2,902 professionals (as of  
31 March 2026) grounded in deep domain expertise across Aerospace, Defence,  
and ESAI.
Outputs We are institutionalising a “Constructor” skill set where traditional engineering 
excellence is fortified by programme ownership, shop-floor capability, and supply-chain 
orchestration. This human capital runway is being further sharpened by a strategic talent 
realignment, including the contracted transfer of approximately 2,200 employees to 
Akkodis to focus our core team on high-margin manufacturing.
Outcomes We have definitively established a non-linear growth engine that decouples revenue 
potential from headcount expansion. This structural shift resulted in record operational 
productivity during the period, with Revenue per Employee rising to  `39.94 Lakh , 
enabling AXISCADES to deliver superior value per professional as we climb toward our 
`9,000 crore revenue target.
Operational Excellence: Shared Infrastructure and Structural Leverage
Primary Capital: Manufactured
Inputs: We deploy strategic capital allocation to bypass “standing start” risks, pivoting 
rapidly toward asset-heavy operations. This is anchored by our investment in physical 
manufacturing and testing assets.
Outputs Our primary output is the build-out of advanced infrastructure at our Atmanirbhar 
capability clusters. This includes a tri-use factory foundation equipped for precision 
machining, advanced composites, and electronics manufacturing, specifically architected 
to serve Aerospace, Defence, and Space programs from a common infrastructure.
Outcomes This shared-use architecture realises structural operating leverage, where common 
facilities shorten programme mobilization and drive down unit costs as production 
volumes scale. This creates a globally scalable platform with a defensible  
manufacturing moat.
Market Leadership: Compounding Relationships and National Pedigree
Primary Capital: Relationships
Inputs: AXISCADES’ relationship capital is built on long-standing executive-level trust with global 
OEMs, deep aerospace certification experience, and strategic alignment with India’s 
national indigenisation priorities under the Atmanirbhar Bharat  initiative.
Outputs Our primary output is the build-out of advanced infrastructure at our Atmanirbhar 
capability clusters. This includes a tri-use factory foundation equipped for precision 
machining, advanced composites, and electronics manufacturing, specifically  
architected to serve Aerospace, Defence, and Space programs from a common 
infrastructure.
Outcomes This shared-use architecture realises structural operating leverage, where common 
facilities shorten programme mobilization and drive down unit costs as production volumes 
scale. This creates a globally scalable platform with a defensible manufacturing moat.

OPERATING ENVIRONMENT AND MARKET LANDSCAPE
Strong demand,   
matching our moats
Aerospace, Defence, semiconductors and Space offer structural opportunity, but qualification, supply, 
capital and timing govern realisation.
AXISCADES participates in four markets with long demand horizons and demanding entry conditions. Commercial-
aircraft backlogs, defence modernisation, AI-led electronics investment and the opening of India’s space ecosystem are 
creating substantial opportunity. However, market scale is only the starting point. In mission-critical industries, opportunity 
becomes revenue only after customer selection, contracting, qualification, supply-chain readiness, delivery, acceptance 
and collection.

Global aviation demand continues to test the capacity of the 
existing fleet and industrial supply chain. Approximately 5.2 billion 
passengers are expected to fly in 2026, 4.4% more than in 2025. 
The preceding year carried nearly five billion passengers across 
38.7 million flights, with passenger traffic increasing by 5.7% and 
the industry-wide load factor reaching a record 83.5%. Air cargo is 
expected to reach 71.6 million tonnes in 2026, an increase of 2.4%.
The longer-term demand profile is equally supportive. IATA expects 
global passenger demand to more than double by 2050, expanding 
at a compound annual rate of approximately 3.1% from 2024 under 
its mid-range scenario. This creates sustained demand not only for 
new aircraft, but also for modification, maintenance, repair, overhaul 
and lifecycle support as existing fleets are utilised more intensively 
and remain in service for longer.
The immediate constraint is production capacity. The global 
commercial-aircraft backlog exceeds 17,000 aircraft, equivalent to 
nearly 12 years of output at current production rates. The backlog 
represents approximately 60% of the active fleet, compared with a 
historical range of 30–40%, while the accumulated delivery shortfall 
is estimated at around 5,300 aircraft. This imbalance is encouraging 
airframers and Tier-1 suppliers to diversify engineering, sourcing 
and manufacturing capacity across a wider qualified supplier base.
The opportunity is therefore not simply to add capacity, but to add 
capacity that can satisfy aerospace certification, traceability, quality 
and delivery requirements. Engine availability, specialised metals 
and composites, critical components, skilled labour and customer approvals continue to constrain production.

The global semiconductor industry is expected to generate 
approximately US$975 billion in sales during 2026. Industry growth 
reached 22% in 2025 and is projected at approximately 26% in 
2026, placing the market on course to exceed US$1 trillion in 2027. 
A separate industry forecast projects growth from US$627 billion 
in 2024 to approximately US$1.03 trillion by 2030, representing a 
compound annual growth rate of 8.6%.
Growth is being led by AI infrastructure, data centres, memory, 
high-performance computing, automotive electronics and industrial 
systems. Server and network chips are projected to expand at 
approximately 11.6% annually to 2030, followed by automotive 
semiconductors at around 10.7%.
The composition of the market is as important as its aggregate 
scale. High-value generative-AI chips account for approximately 
half of semiconductor revenue while representing less than 0.2% 
of unit volumes. Approximately 1.05 trillion chips were sold during 
2025 at an average selling price of US$0.74, while generative-
AI accelerators represented fewer than 20 million units. This 
concentration illustrates why value is migrating towards high-
performance design, memory, interconnect, thermal management, 
testing and the complete hardware systems surrounding the chip.
India’s near-term advantage lies in this wider value chain. 
The country accounts for approximately 20% of the global 
semiconductor-design workforce, while domestic semiconductor 
demand is projected to grow at approximately 19% annually 
and reach around US$90 billion by FY2030. Design, embedded 
systems, assembly, packaging, testing, electronics manufacturing and system-level integration therefore 
present more immediate opportunities than 
leading-edge fabrication.
AXISCADES participates in this “value 
around the chip” through electronics

hardware realisation and AI-enabled 
products. Its relevance depends on 
converting engineering knowledge into 
prototypes, validated hardware and repeat

One demand pattern across four markets
Although the four markets differ in customers, technologies and 
procurement structures, they share a common demand pattern. 
Customers require additional qualified capacity, more resilient 
supply chains, faster product development and greater domestic 
capability. At the same time, technology content and system 
complexity are increasing, while the financial and operational 
consequences of failure remain high.
This makes connected capability increasingly valuable. A supplier 
able to link engineering, electronics, industrialisation, manufacturing, 
testing and lifecycle support can reduce the number of interfaces 
a customer must manage and retain learning across successive 
programme stages. The same capability foundation, including 
precision manufacturing, composites, electronics, embedded 
computing, testing and systems engineering, can also support 
selected requirements across Aerospace, Defence and Space.
The constraints are similarly connected. Specialised materials 
and electronic components can be scarce. Certification, security 
clearance and customer approval limit the speed at which new 
capacity can enter a supply chain. Skilled talent is concentrated, 
while procurement, inspection and acceptance schedules can shift. 
These characteristics create long demand horizons but can also 
produce non-linear quarterly outcomes.
FY2026 demonstrated this distinction. Approximately `142 crore of 
anticipated revenue was not recognised before year-end because 
of supply-chain interruptions, input availability, programme 
scheduling and transaction-related factors. The underlying orders 
remained, but the timing shift affected reported revenue, EBITDA 
and cash conversion. Market opportunity therefore needs to be 
read together with execution evidence.
India’s expanding role
India’s position is advancing from engineering and talent 
support towards a broader role in design, industrialisation and 
manufacturing. Global aerospace customers are diversifying supply 
chains. Defence procurement increasingly favours domestic design 
and production. Semiconductor initiatives are building capacity 
around design, packaging, testing and systems. Space reform is 
allowing private participation across satellite, launch-support and 
ground-segment activities.
For AXISCADES, the opportunity is strongest where these 
national tailwinds meet capabilities already established within the 
Company or capable of disciplined extension. India’s cost and 
talent advantages create an entry point, but sustained participation 
will depend on certification, intellectual property, quality, delivery 
performance and the ability to support customers throughout a 
programme lifecycle.
How AXISCADES selects from the opportunity
The Company applies a staged screen to opportunities across 
strategic fit, customer relevance, capability adjacency, qualification 
burden, capital requirement, working-capital profile and risk-
adjusted return.Partnership-led entry is appropriate where 
technology, certification or market access 
is complementary. Direct investment 
becomes more relevant where customer 
demand is qualified, programme ownership 
is clear and capability can be shared 
across multiple customers or Platforms. 
Emerging opportunities are progressed 
through defined technical, commercial and 
capital gates, preserving flexibility until the 
evidence supports further scale.
This discipline is particularly important in 
Space and AI, where market narratives 
can move ahead of commercial maturity. 
AXISCADES’ participation is therefore 
defined through specific outcomes in 
hardware, electronics, testing, thermal 
systems, ground infrastructure or domain-
led AI rather than through just broad market 
association.

STRATEGIC PRIORITIES
Five priorities for focused 
value creation 
The priorities translate AXISCADES 3.0 into choices about Platform scale, products, 
capacity, cash and organisational control.
AXISCADES 3.0 is the operating expression of the Company’s 
strategic ambition. It is intended to narrow attention towards high-
value Platforms, extend engineering into products and systems, build 
reusable capability and make capital deployment more selective. Five 
priorities organise that work.These five strategic priorities are fundamental to AXISCADES 3.0 as they collectively architect a definitive transition 
from a manpower-intensive “architect” of engineering services to a high-margin, product-led “constructor” of 
mission-ready systems. By narrowing institutional focus toward four structurally supported growth platforms, the 
Group ensures specialised capital deployment and clearer performance accountability across its most potent 
demand streams. This structural shift is institutionalised through a shared tri-use manufacturing foundation at our 
Atmanirbhar clusters, which generates non-linear operating leverage by serving Aerospace, Defence, and Space 
from a common, modular infrastructure. Crucially, the systematic reallocation of approximately `2,256 crore in 
proceeds from legacy divestments into this deep-tech engine provides the robust funding required to fully transition 
the business model and accelerate our trajectory toward the visionary Power 930 revenue and profit targets. 
Finally, strengthening our execution framework and mirroring architecture ensures this rapid scaling is supported 
by rigorous programme ownership and governance, effectively de-risking our evolution into a globally scalable 
manufacturing powerhouse.
1. Scale Focused Platforms
We are concentrating leadership attention and capital investment 
into four distinct growth engines: Aerospace Manufacturing, 
SCM & MRO; Defence Solutions; XiDA Inc (the AI-centric ESAI 
Platform); and our newly formed Space division. This structural 
narrowing allows for specialised resource deployment and 
greater accountability. Following the successful realignment of 
our portfolio, these four pure-play manufacturing and deep-tech 
engines now form the core of our future performance disclosure.
2. Move from Effort to Owned Outcomes
The Group is aggressively transitioning from being a service-
led “architect” of designs to a product-led “constructor” of 
mission-ready assemblies. This shift requires taking full-cycle 
responsibility across design, qualification, industrialisation, 
manufacturing, integration, and sustainment. For AXISCADES, 
productisation does not mean abandoning our engineering 
heritage; it means converting sixteen years of domain 
knowledge into repeatable deliverables, embedded intellectual 
property (IP), and recurring participation across the entire 
product lifecycle.
3. Build Shared, Flexible Capability
Our manufacturing strategy is anchored in a common 
technology foundation. We utilise “tri-use” infrastructure—such 
as strategic electronics, automated test systems, precision 
machining, and advanced composites—that serves Aerospace, 
Defence, and Space simultaneously. This shared architecture at 
our Devanahalli (DAC) and Missile (MAC) Atmanirbhar clusters 
ensures high asset utilisation and structural operating leverage. 
Capacity is expanded through modular phases, strictly released 
against qualified customer demand and visible programme 
milestones to preserve capital efficiency.4. Capital Reallocation for 
Strategic Scale
We are systematically deploying the 
~`2,256 crore in proceeds from our 
strategic divestment programme to 
definitively transition AXISCADES toward 
a high-margin, pure-play technology and 
manufacturing engine. This priority moves 
the Group away from legacy, manpower-
intensive engineering services to fully 
fund the “Power 930” organic capex and 
inorganic M&A pipeline. By concentrating 
our capital base on deep-tech platforms 
where we possess a defensible technical 
moat, we ensure that every rupee invested 
directly accelerates our trajectory toward the 
`9,000 crore revenue milestone for FY2030.
5. Strengthen the Execution 
Organisation
To support an asset-heavy manufacturing 
mandate, we are re-architecting our talent 
and governance frameworks. This involves 
developing deep capabilities in product 
ownership, shop-floor management, 
industrial relations, and supply-chain 
orchestration. This discipline extends to our 
inorganic strategy, where every acquisition 
integrates through a defined “Mirroring 
Architecture”. By embedding AXISCADES’ 
leadership and financial controls into 
acquired entities from day one, we ensure 
seamless performance visibility and the 
protection of Group-wide margins.

specialised international capability to bypass “standing start” risks.
• Organic Asset Build-out (Atmanirbhar Clusters):  A significant portion of capital is dedicated to our

AXISCADES’ rigorous India operating model into international entities while embedding their specialised 
capabilities back into our India platforms for global scale. Our current pipeline includes four key targets: one 
in India for domestic aerospace consolidation, two in the US for AI-native engineering via XiDA Inc, and one in 
Europe for OEM supply chain integration.

Capital allocation in Aerospace and Defence differs from many conventional industries. Customers often require 
evidence of land, equipment, process, people, quality systems and first-article capability before larger orders are 
placed. AXISCADES may therefore need to deploy some capital before the associated revenue is contracted or 
recognised. The challenge is to build enough evidence to win without building so much that the asset becomes 
stranded.
Customer involvement narrows this uncertainty. Equipment specifications, approved sources, qualification plans, 
bill-of-material decisions and inspection criteria can all provide proof that the investment is connected to a real 
programme pathway. Flexible assets and shared capability provide a second layer of protection where customer 
and security requirements permit.

liquidity. As our manufacturing footprint expands, AXISCADES has allocated approximately `156 crore of the

Market Landscape: Capitalising on Indigenisation and Procurement Reform
The addressable opportunity in the Indian defence sector is structurally supported by a robust domestic 
procurement framework. India’s defence budget for 2025-26 stands at `6.81 lakh crore, with approximately 75% 
of the capital acquisition budget earmarked for domestic sourcing. Furthermore, Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) 
approvals totalling `3.3 to 3.6 trillion were accorded during FY2026, creating a predictable pipeline for conversion 
into executable orders over the next two to four years. Government mandates, including the Positive Indigenisation 
Lists and the Technology Transfer Policy, are compelling OEMs to localise design and intellectual property, shifting 
significant value from build-to-print activities toward the high-end systems integration and digital R&D domains 
where AXISCADES is surgically positioned.
Strategic Focus Areas: Delivering the Integrated Defence Proposition
Our Defence roadmap is architected around four high-fidelity focus areas, each designed to capture recurring value 
across the entire product lifecycle:
• Missile Integration & Ground Systems:  Providing end-to-end support for national missile programmes, 
including electronics, communication subsystems, and ground integration. The Group holds sole-source 
positions on critical platforms, including support for the Akash, Pinaka, and Astra programmes.
• Radar Manufacturing & Strategic Electronics: Converting design wins into certified production for AESA 
radars, signal processing units, and avionics suites. Our expertise covers mission-critical electronics for fighter 
aircraft upgrades and naval electronic warfare platforms.
• Unmanned Combat Systems & Counter-UAS:  Developing sovereign platforms for unmanned warfare and 
man-portable countermeasures. This segment is an emerging national priority, and AXISCADES is building 
deeper capability across hardkill, softkill, and directed energy weapons.
• Maintenance & Lifecycle Support:  Closing the loop through Defence MRO and performance-based logistics 
(PBL) to ensure the long-term sustainment of integrated national platforms.

What is XiDA?
XiDA Inc. is AXISCADES’ US-based, AI-centric platform established to lead the Group’s aggressive expansion 
into the global Electronics, Semiconductor, and Artificial Intelligence (ESAI) markets. The strategic thinking behind 
setting up this structure is to create a dedicated “Mirroring Architecture” vehicle that allows the Group to bypass 
“standing start” risks by acquiring specialized AI-native engineering capabilities and securing immediate access to 
Tier-1 technology customers in the United States. This structure works more effectively by serving as a bridge for 
international M&A; it enables AXISCADES to acquire advanced deep-tech intellectual property abroad and then 
deploy those high-value competencies into its manufacturing clusters for global scale. By institutionalizing this flow 
of international capability into a domestic manufacturing foundation, XiDA accelerates the Group’s transition into a 
product-led powerhouse, ensuring that revenue growth is driven by repeatable IP rather than headcount expansion.
Market Opportunity: The US$90 Billion Semiconductor and AI Super-Cycle
The addressable opportunity for AXISCADES in the ESAI sector is underpinned by a profound structural shift 
in the global technology landscape. India’s semiconductor demand is projected to compound at 19% to reach 
approximately US$90 billion by FY2030, supported by a workforce that already accounts for one-fifth of the global 
semiconductor design talent. Simultaneously, the emergence of “Physical AI” - where intelligence is embedded 
directly into hardware - is creating a multi-trillion dollar market. Locally, the Indian AI industry is expected to reach 
US$28.8 billion by the close of the reporting period, growing at a CAGR of 45%. AXISCADES is uniquely positioned 
at the intersection of these trends, providing the critical bridge between chip design and mission-critical product 
implementation for hyperscalers and global OEMs.

technology lifecycle:

infrastructure for hyperscale data centres, supporting the massive compute requirements of Generative AI.
• Electronic Hardware-Driven Physical AI: Developing autonomous robotics platforms and intelligent 
hardware where AI is embedded directly at the edge.
• Semiconductor & Electronics Manufacturing Test Systems: Providing validation platforms and integrated 
test solutions for semiconductor manufacturing equipment OEMs.
• Assembly Line Subsystems for Global OEMs:  Engineering production subsystems and automation 
modules for industrial-scale manufacturing.Infrastructure: The Aeroland Innovation Hub

engineering and leadership teams, housing specialized centres of excellence for high-reliability electronics 
and system integration. By co-locating our AI-native engineering teams with our digital manufacturing

customer acceptance, invoicing, collection

The conversion chain: design, prove, build, scale
The productisation model can be understood as a sequence of evidence gates. Engineering knowledge creates the 
initial design; prototypes and testing establish technical credibility; customer qualification and first-article approval 
make the output acceptable for a programme; manufacturing, supply-chain orchestration and inspection make 
it repeatable; and lifecycle support, configuration control and intellectual property reuse determine whether the 
economics can scale.
• Design: Identify a repeatable customer requirement and retain 
the architecture, know-how and programme learning that can 
support future work.
• Prove:  Move through prototyping, verification, testing, 
configuration control and customer qualification, recognising 
that mission-critical markets reward evidence rather than intent.
• Build:  Connect tooling, electronics manufacturing, precision 
production, quality, supply planning and inspection so that a 
technically successful design can be delivered reliably.
• Scale:  Extend from a first programme into repeat production, 
adjacent platforms, lifecycle support or reusable modules, while 
protecting margin and cash conversion.The next proof point is 
repeatability
FY2026 established the productisation 
architecture: a stronger programme 
pipeline, deeper domain capability, initial 
manufacturing and testing infrastructure, 
and a clearer route from engineering into 
products and systems. The next proof point 
is repeatability: qualification, product and 
solutions revenue, reusable architectures, 
accepted deliveries, cash generation and 
returns on capital.
Late events during Q1 FY2027  further 
formalised the AI-centric ESAI platform and 
strategic-platform organisation. They inform 
the direction of travel but are not FY2026 
performance; FY2026 established the 
technology base and made productisation 
more visible. Productisation is the point at which engineering 
knowledge becomes a repeatable, qualified and 
ownable outcome.Productisation begins where design becomes ownership
The Company’s long-term ambition is to move towards a greater contribution from products, solutions and 
manufacturing-linked programmes. The economic value increases when AXISCADES retains design knowledge, 
carries responsibility through validation and industrialisation, and participates in repeat production, systems 
integration or lifecycle support. That is the point at which intellectual capital begins to produce operating leverage 
and a revenue opportunity that is less directly linked to additional headcount.
One technology spine across four strategic domains
• Aerospace:  FY2026 expanded the Company’s role beyond engineering services into aerospace tooling, 
tool design and an end-to-end electrical wire interconnection system programme combining design, tooling, 
prototyping and manufacturing. The capability base is intended to extend into precision manufacturing, 
composites, supply-chain support and component lifecycle services, where qualification and customer trust 
create higher barriers to entry.
• Defence:  The Company recorded 21 consolidated design and programme wins during FY2026 across radar, 
electronic warfare, missile and countermeasure systems, platform electronics and integrated solutions. The 
operating ambition is to convert these positions into qualified production, subsystem supply and complete-
system responsibility, supported by systems engineering, electronics, harnesses, testing and manufacturing 
capability.
• ESAI: The Electronics, Semiconductors and Artificial Intelligence platform is being organised around the 
value around the chip: post-silicon engineering, embedded systems, electronics manufacturing, testing, AI-
enabled products and hardware realisation. During FY2026, the EMS facility and acoustic testing laboratory 
at Devanahalli Aero Land became operational, giving the platform a physical route from design to validated 
hardware.
• Space:  Space was established as a distinct strategic direction because its technology cycles, regulatory 
requirements, partnerships and procurement models differ from conventional Aerospace. FY2026 activity 
focused on preparatory capability: discussions with global space primes for satellite-bus manufacturing and 
integration, and an initial partnership for terrestrial space-situational-awareness capability. Space remains an 
emerging Platform with no separately disclosed FY2026 revenue.TECHNOLOGY , INNOVATION AND PRODUCTISATION

Human capital as a strategic asset
The strategic shift described in “Sharper by Design” changes the capability equation. Engineering depth remains 
central, but product-led and manufacturing-led growth also requires industrialisation, production, quality, supply-

understand not only the task assigned to it, but the dependencies around that task and the customer outcome to

That change was visible in the FY2026 numbers. Group headcount increased from 2,891 to 2,902, or approximately 
0.4%, while revenue from operations increased by 12.4%. The resulting revenue per employee of `39.94 lakh is an 
indicator of operating leverage, although it should not be read as a measure of individual performance. It shows 
that the Company’s value-creation challenge is increasingly about capability mix, utilisation, programme ownership 
and repeatable execution rather than headcount growth alone.

Culture and continuity during portfolio change

The Company believes that the divested activity serves different 
customers and capabilities from the Defence and electronics 
delivery organisations, limiting direct overlap. The principal

communication distinguishes what is decided from what remains

identifies where employees can obtain answers. Manager capability

Skills, certification and careers

PARTNERSHIPS AND CUSTOMER RELATIONSHIPS
Trust is an execution asset 
Long-cycle programmes reward relationships built on technical relevance, transparent 
commitments and reliable delivery.Ecosystem participation
The standalone BRSR identifies participation in NASSCOM, the 
Society of Indian Aerospace Technologies and Industries, the 
Hanseatic Engineering & Consulting Association e.V., Hamburg 
Aviation and the Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers. These 
forums help the Company understand policy, technology, talent and 
supply-chain developments across its markets.
Relationship quality as a managed outcome
Customer satisfaction, repeat business, programme continuity, 
supplier quality, corrective-action closure and joint-development 
milestones provide evidence of relationship quality. These 
indicators must sit alongside sales pipeline measures. A large 
opportunity with weak alignment is not a stronger relationship.
Relationships across the programme lifecycle
The purpose of a relationship changes as a programme 
matures. During opportunity definition, the priority is an honest 
understanding of the need and decision path. During design and 
qualification, it is rapid technical access and clear ownership. 
During production, it is demand visibility, supply, quality and 
acceptance. During sustainment, it is availability, configuration and 
field learning. Relationship management must follow this lifecycle.
A single customer may engage AXISCADES across more than 
one geography or capability. A coordinated account view can 
identify adjacencies, but expansion should be earned through 
performance. The Company should not allow cross-selling 
ambition to blur the accountable programme owner or overstate the 
readiness of a new capability.
Customer-backed investment
In Aerospace and Defence, capability may need to exist before full-
rate orders are placed. Customer evidence can take several forms: 
a defined qualification path, approved source status, forecast 
demand, long-term agreement, development funding, tooling 
support or co-investment. The strength of that evidence should 
influence the amount and timing of AXISCADES capital.
This does not transfer investment responsibility to the customer. It 
makes assumptions visible. The Company still needs a downside 
case, alternative uses for the asset, supply and people readiness, 
working-capital capacity and a return threshold. Customer backing 
is a gate, not a guarantee.
Build a programme-ready supply ecosystem
Suppliers extend AXISCADES’ quality, capacity and resilience. 
Selection should consider technical capability, process control, 
lead time, financial health, cybersecurity, labour and environmental 
practices, continuity and the ability to provide traceable evidence. 
Critical sources need development plans and, where practical, 
qualified alternatives.
Localisation can reduce exposure and build national capability, 
but only if local output meets the same programme requirements. AXISCADES can support suppliers through 
clearer forecasts, technical guidance, 
quality planning and joint corrective action. 
The benefit is not simply lower input 
cost; it is a more reliable and responsive 
programme system.
Govern partnerships for the 
hard moments
Partnership documents should define 
contributions, decision rights, economics, 
intellectual property, data, quality, customer 
ownership, compliance, liability, exit and 
dispute resolution. These provisions 
matter most when a milestone is missed, a 
product changes or a market assumption 
fails. Governance should make the difficult 
decision faster rather than preserve 
ambiguity.
Relationship health is therefore evidenced 
by repeat work, milestone reliability, 
issue-closure time, supplier performance, 
customer satisfaction, joint-development 
progress and the quality of escalation. For 
stakeholders, trust has practical value: 
it reduces friction, makes investment 
evidence stronger and improves 
programme velocity.

Infrastructure is the bridge from engineering to industrial value

model. Product-led growth depends on the ability to prototype, test, industrialise, manufacture, integrate, inspect 
and support defined outputs. These activities require equipment, laboratories, tooling, production systems, quality 
controls, supply-chain coordination and people with the capability to operate them consistently.
The Company’s infrastructure thesis is based on a common technology spine. Precision machining, advanced 
composites, electronics assembly, mission-critical electronics, testing, tooling, systems engineering and integration 
have relevance across Aerospace, Defence and selected Space applications. The same asset can therefore 
support more than one Platform when customer segregation, security, configuration control and certification 
requirements are preserved. This creates the potential for better utilisation, faster mobilisation and the transfer of 
learning across programmes.

Designed for flexible, high-complexity production
The planned production environment is being designed for flexibility 
rather than single-product dedication. Automation, smart fixturing, 
digital work instructions, virtual build and rapid changeover can 
support repeatable production while allowing equipment to be used 
across programmes. Virtual build and digital process definition 
can identify manufacturability issues before physical production, 
reducing rework and shortening the path from design to an 
accepted first article.
Flexibility does not mean removing controls. Mission-critical 
programmes require controlled access, customer-data protection, 
configuration discipline, approved materials, traceability, inspection 
evidence and clear segregation where security or certification 
requires it. Shared infrastructure is therefore being designed as 
common capacity with deliberate boundaries, rather than as 
undifferentiated floor space.
Capital intensity with a conversion test
Capital expenditure increased to `134.44 crore in FY2026 from 
`37.90 crore in FY2025, while capital work in progress stood at 
`44.22 crore at year-end. The increase reflects an active phase of 
capacity and capability creation. It also makes the return profile of 
the infrastructure programme an important part of the Company’s

MATERIAL MATTERS FOR LONG-TERM VALUE
The issues that can change 
the outcome
Material matters connect stakeholder expectations with the strategic, operating and ESG 
factors most capable of affecting value.
AXISCADES considers a matter material when it can 
significantly affect enterprise value, stakeholder outcomes 
or both. The working view below brings together 
the FY2026 BRSR process, management priorities 
and principal risks. It is intended to focus decisions, 
ownership and disclosure.
How materiality informs decisions
Stakeholder surveys, direct interactions, programme feedback, regulatory requirements, risk reviews and 
management judgement inform the assessment. Matters are considered across short-, medium- and long-term 
horizons and through four tests: scale of impact, likelihood or exposure, strategic relevance and stakeholder concern.
