7.0 Principal risks, concerns and mitigation 
measures
AXISCADES entered FY2027 with a clearer strategic perimeter 
and a more demanding operating model. The Company is moving 
from a broad engineering-services portfolio towards Aerospace 
Manufacturing, Defence Solutions, ESAI and AI, and selected Space 
opportunities. This sharpens the value-creation logic, but also 
concentrates execution risk around transaction completion, programme 
conversion, capacity commissioning, supply-chain resilience, quality, 
integration and cash generation.
The assessment below distinguishes audited FY2026 evidence 
from material developments announced after 31 March 2026. At the 
reporting date, no divestment proceeds had been received and no 
contribution from proposed acquisitions had been recognised.
7.1 Portfolio transition, transaction proceeds and separation
The two-phase Engineering Services Divestment Programme, 
announced after the reporting date, is central to the Company’s 
portfolio reshaping and future capital allocation. Completion remains 
subject to conditions precedent, regulatory approvals, closing 
adjustments and agreed timelines. Part of the consideration is 
contingent on future performance, while the amount available for 
reinvestment will depend on taxes, transaction costs, adjustments, 
exchange rates and the timing of actual cash receipts. Announced 
transaction value therefore does not represent immediately available 
funding.
Separation creates a second layer of risk. The risk lies in transferring 
employees, systems and enabling functions without weakening 
customer delivery, programme ownership, data integrity, certification 
knowledge or financial control. Transitional service arrangements 
may also leave temporary or stranded overheads within the retained 
Company.
Mitigation measures:  The response centres on a single transaction 
and separation plan covering conditions, approvals, cash-flow 
sensitivities and Board gates. Capital deployment will be aligned with 
cash received rather than announced consideration. Customer and 
programme accountability, system access, service levels, employee 
transfers, knowledge retention and stranded-cost removal will be 
tracked against named owners and milestones.
7.2 Programme conversion, supply chain and cash generation
The central operating risk is the conversion of opportunity into 
revenue and cash. Management reported that approximately `142 
crore of fourth-quarter deliverables could not be recognised before 
year-end because of supply-chain constraints, programme timing, 
inspection and acceptance schedules, and transaction-related 
factors. The associated earnings were not recognised in FY2026 and 
remain subject to delivery, inspection, customer acceptance and the 
applicable accounting criteria.The 27 May 2026 operating baseline included `927 
crore of orders under execution, `285 crore of Assured 
Forecast Visibility and two L1 positions awaiting 
contract award. These categories carry different levels 
of certainty. AFV reflects qualified programme positions 
and customer forecasts; L1 status is not a contract; and 
neither is included in the firm order book.
Mitigation measures:  Management’s response 
focuses on the programme-level order-to-cash chain, 
from commercial commitment and procurement 
coverage through production, inspection, acceptance, 
invoicing and collection. The CRM initiative begun 
during FY2026 provides a foundation for broader 
workflow integration. Immediate priorities include 
critical-material coverage, alternative sourcing where 
technically possible, earlier booking of inspection 
and acceptance slots, configuration control and 
collection governance. Key leading indicators 
include procurement coverage, work-in-progress and 
acceptance ageing, billing milestones, receivable days, 
inventory turns and operating cash flow.
7.3 Capacity commissioning and capital 
discipline
The move into manufacturing, testing, integration 
and MRO requires capacity ahead of revenue. This 
creates exposure to construction delays, equipment 
commissioning, certification, staffing, utilisation and 
return on invested capital. If capacity is commissioned 
before qualified demand is ready, depreciation and 
fixed costs can rise without a corresponding revenue 
contribution. If commissioning is late, programme 
conversion can be delayed.
During FY2026, Devanahalli Aero Land was fitted 
out and the move into the facility commenced. 
Groundbreaking and civil work also began at the 
Devanahalli Atmanirbhar Complex, while land for 
the Missile Atmanirbhar Complex was acquired. 
Subsequent commissioning targets are forward-looking 
and remain dependent on approved programme 
demand.
Mitigation measures:  Investment will be released 
in phases and linked to customer-backed load, 
certification milestones and clear utilisation thresholds. 
Equipment and tooling will be commissioned line 
by line, with cost-to-complete, schedule variance, 
qualified load, yield, utilisation and return hurdles 
reviewed together. Shared use across Aerospace, 
Defence and selected Space applications can improve 
capital efficiency, but only where technical, quality and 
regulatory requirements genuinely permit it.
7.4 Acquisition execution and integration
The Company is contemplating 3-4 acquisition 
targets across India, the United States and Europe. Management indicated that three planned acquisitions were 
targeted for FY2027, with the wider pipeline extending into FY2028. 
These are opportunities, not completed transactions. Each 
remains subject to due diligence, valuation, definitive agreements, 
approvals, financing, completion and the establishment of control.
Multiple transactions in a compressed period can strain 
management capacity and create valuation, customer-retention, 
cultural, systems, governance and key-person risks. The proposed 
“mirroring” model may accelerate integration, but it is not a 
substitute for entity-specific diligence and operating design.
Mitigation measures:  Transaction quality takes precedence over 
transaction count. Each acquisition will be subject to independent 
valuation, downside analysis, full financial, tax, legal, technical 
and customer diligence, a clearly accountable integration leader, 
retention plans and a practical 100-day agenda. No revenue, 
earnings or capability contribution is assumed before completion 
and control are established. Integration will be sequenced against 
the Company’s capacity to absorb change.
7.5 Quality, certification and contract execution
As AXISCADES takes greater responsibility for manufacturing and 
complete-system delivery, quality and certification become direct 
economic risks. Supplier quality, first-pass yield, non-conformance, 
configuration management, product liability, warranty exposure and 
customer acceptance can affect revenue, margins, cash flow and 
reputation. Long qualification cycles can also delay the movement 
from design win to repeat production.
Fixed-price and milestone-based programmes add estimation 
risk. Weak bid discipline, scope change or inaccurate estimates 
at completion can erode margins, while incomplete acceptance 
evidence can delay revenue recognition and collection.
Mitigation measures: The control framework centres on bid and 
design reviews, supplier qualification, independent inspection, 
stage-gate controls and disciplined change management ahead 
of production ramp-up. Programme reviews connect quality 
indicators with estimates at completion, contract-loss assessment, 
acceptance evidence and cash milestones. The operating 
dashboard tracks first-pass yield, non-conformance closure, audit 
findings, certification status, claims and warranty trends.
7.6 Customer, market, geopolitical and currency exposure
The Group retains exposure to a relatively concentrated set of 
large customers and long-cycle programmes. Customer budgets, 
procurement policy, programme reprioritisation and acceptance 
timing can affect order conversion and revenue. Export controls, 
sanctions, tariffs, geopolitical disruption and restrictions on 
strategic technologies can affect market access and the availability 
of specialised materials or electronics.
The geographic revenue mix across APAC, Europe, the United 
States and Canada provides some diversification, but does not 
remove customer, programme or trade-policy concentration. 
Foreign-currency revenue also creates translation and transaction 
exposure.Mitigation measures: The response combines continued 
diversification by customer, platform and geography 
with exposure limits and scenario analysis for material 
programmes. Contract reviews cover indexation, change 
control, liability, export restrictions and termination rights. 
Natural operating hedges and approved financial hedging 
operate within the Company’s treasury policy, supported by 
consistent restricted-party screening, licence management 
and programme classification across facilities.
7.7 Technology, cybersecurity and  
intellectual property
AXISCADES operates in domains involving sensitive 
customer data, strategic electronics, embedded software, 
semiconductor engineering and artificial intelligence. A 
cyber incident, loss of intellectual property, unauthorised 
access or third-party vulnerability could disrupt delivery, 
compromise customer trust and create legal or national-
security consequences. Rapid technology cycles also 
create a risk that assets, products or skills become 
obsolete before generating adequate returns.
Mitigation measures: The control approach embeds 
secure development, least-privilege access, network 
and data segregation, continuous monitoring, incident 
response and third-party assurance in programme delivery. 
Technology investment is staged against customer 
roadmaps, reusable architectures and clear qualification 
pathways. Cyber, intellectual-property and obsolescence 
risks are assessed before acquisitions, partnerships and 
new facilities are integrated.
7.8 Talent and organisational continuity
The reported attrition rate at the end of FY2026 was 
19%. The portfolio transition also requires the movement 
or rebuilding of enabling functions, while the retained 
Company will require deeper skills in manufacturing, 
programme management, supply chain, quality, 
certification and systems integration. Gaps in leadership, 
succession or knowledge transfer could affect delivery and 
customer continuity.
Mitigation measures: The people response focuses on 
mapping critical roles and programme knowledge before 
separation or integration; aligning succession, retention 
and structured handovers with commissioning and 
customer milestones; and establishing clear ownership, 
backup capability and targeted training for each strategic 
programme.
7.9 Reporting perimeter and investor comparability
The FY2027 operating and reporting perimeter is expected 
to differ materially from FY2026. Divestments retained 
economic interests and any completed acquisitions may 
affect the classification of continuing and discontinued 
operations, consolidation dates, margins, capital employed 
and cash flow. Without a clear bridge, investors may 
misread the economics of the transformed Company.MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION & ANALYSIS

Mitigation measures:  The response combines transaction-specific

FY2027 control priorities
The FY2027 risk agenda will be assessed against a short set of 
operating outcomes:
• Transactions completed only after all conditions, approvals 
and disclosure controls are satisfied, with capital deployed 
against net cash received.
• Executable programmes and year-end carry-forward

• Capacity commissioned against qualified demand, with

reported perimeter to the FY2027 continuing business.
Risk governance
The Company’s enterprise risk framework is overseen by the 
Board and the Risk Management Committee, with additional 
Audit Committee oversight of financial risks and controls. As the 
business model changes, risk management is moving closer to 
the programme level. A connected dashboard will bring together 
transaction milestones, committed capital, order conversion, 
cash, capacity, quality, people and customer continuity, with clear 
escalation thresholds and accountable owners.
This integrated approach is consistent with the “Built the Runway” 
strategy. Strategic focus will create value only if risk signals are 
identified early, capital is released selectively and operating 
interventions occur before delivery variance becomes a financial 
outcome.
8. Internal Control Systems and Their Adequacy
The Company has adopted policies and procedures to ensure the 
orderly and efficient conduct of its business, including adherence 
to Company policies, the safeguarding of its assets, the prevention 
and detection of fraud and errors, the accuracy and completeness of accounting records, and the timely preparation 
of reliable financial disclosures. These controls are 
aligned with statutory requirements and industry 
practice, covering the critical aspects of operations and 
compliance.
Governance and oversight. The Audit Committee 
reviews the adequacy of internal control systems, the 
adequacy and structure of the internal audit function, 
the scope of work discussed with internal and statutory 
auditors, the effectiveness of the audit process, the 
independence and performance of both sets of 
auditors, internal audit findings, and any weakness 
or failure of internal control systems reported by 
auditors. The Committee separately evaluates internal 
financial controls and the risk management system. 
Internal audit is conducted by an independent firm of 
consultants, and the statutory audit by an independent 
firm of chartered accountants, both reporting to the 
Committee.
Assurance.  The statutory auditors obtain an 
understanding of internal control relevant to the audit 
in order to design appropriate audit procedures, and 
under Section 143(3)(i) of the Companies Act, 2013, 
express an opinion on whether the Company has 
adequate internal financial controls with reference to 
financial statements in place and on the operating 
effectiveness of those controls. Significant deficiencies 
in internal control identified during the audit are 
communicated to those charged with governance. The 
audited financial results for the year ended 31 March 
2026 were reviewed by the Audit Committee and 
approved by the Board of Directors on 27 May 2026.
Vigil mechanism.  The Company’s vigil mechanism, 
which incorporates the whistleblower policy, provides 
a formal route for all Directors and employees to 
approach the Chairman of the Audit Committee 
and make protected disclosures about unethical 
behaviour, actual or suspected fraud, or violations 
of the Company’s Code of Conduct or ethics policy. 
Disclosures are addressed in the manner and time 
frames prescribed in the policy. No personnel were 
denied access to the Chairman of the Audit Committee 
during the year.
Evolution of the control environment during 
FY2026.  The scope and complexity of the control 
environment expanded materially during the year. 
The Group comprised sixteen consolidated entities 
and one associate at the year end, spanning six 
countries. The shift from engineering services delivery 
toward manufacturing brought inventory, production 
and supply chain controls into greater prominence, 
with inventories rising to `78.97 crore and materials 
consumed to `253.36 crore. Capital expenditure of 
`134.44 crore, against `37.90 crore in the prior year, 
placed corresponding weight on project authorisation, contractor management and capitalisation controls, with capital 
work in progress of `44.22 crore carried at the year-end.
Controls over estimation and provisioning were exercised across 
several judgements during the year. The Group assessed the 
financial implications of the four Labour Codes notified on 21 
November 2025, recognising an increase in gratuity and leave 
liability of `7.82 crore arising from past service cost. Impairment 
assessments were carried out on goodwill against identified 
impairment indicators, resulting in a charge of `7.98 crore, and 
contingent purchase consideration was remeasured against actual 
subsidiary performance, producing a gain of `4.63 crore. Provision 
for expected credit losses on trade receivables and contract assets 
was `3.77 crore, against `2.21 crore in the prior year, and provision 
for foreseeable loss on contracts was `2.79 crore against `1.99 
crore, both reflecting the increase in receivables and in contracted 
manufacturing work.

to 61.8% in Q4. This is an intra-year comparison rather than an 
FY2025-to-FY2026 movement.
The reported attrition rate ended FY2026 at 19%, unchanged from 
Q1 and one percentage point below the Q2 and Q3 levels. The 
Company responded through employee-engagement, upskilling 
and career-mapping programmes. Employee well-being initiatives, 
described in the FY2026 BRSR report in this annual report, include 
online medical consultations for employees and their families, an 
Employee Assistance Programme, health and wellness webinars, 
a structured meal programme and formal grievance-redressal 
mechanisms.
Technical capability building covered aerostructures, product 
lifecycle management, computer-aided engineering, manufacturing engineering and tool design. Leadership depth also 
increased through the addition of strategy, growth and 
investor-relations capability. On 27 March 2026, Mr 
Giridhar Aramane was appointed as a Non-Executive 
Independent Director, bringing more than three 
decades of experience across defence, infrastructure, 
finance and public policy. Employee stock-option and 
share-based-payment disclosures are cross-referenced 
to the statutory sections of the Annual Report.
9.2 Productivity and Non-Linear Growth
Consolidated revenue increased by 12.4% in FY2026, 
while closing headcount increased by 0.4%. The 
resulting indicators point to improved operating 
leverage. These are one-year indicators rather than 
evidence of structural decoupling, and are influenced 
by business mix, utilisation, currency, programme 
timing and the use of closing rather than average 
headcount.
Measure FY2026 FY2025 Change
Revenue per employee `39.94 lakh `35.65 lakh +12.0 %
EBITDA per employee `6.12 lakh `4.93 lakh +24.1%
Employee benefits expense / revenue 47.84% 50.10% (227) bps
EBITDA per employee increased faster than revenue per employee, 
while employee benefits expense declined by approximately 227 
basis points as a share of revenue. This indicates better people-
cost absorption in FY2026. Comparability will change in FY2027 as 
employees aligned with the divested businesses transfer with those 
businesses, subject to transaction completion and the applicable 
employee-transfer arrangements.
9.3 Preparing the People Model for Manufacturing
During FY2026, the operating model remained predominantly 
engineering- and project-led. As the Company moves further into 
manufacturing, the people agenda is expected to widen to include 
shop-floor workforce planning, workmen skill certification, industrial 
relations, productivity monitoring and standardised quality and 
safety practices.Late event during the first quarter of FY2027. 
Following the reporting date, management outlined 
a manufacturing-workforce framework that includes 
building shop-floor and industrial-relations capability, 
establishing a dedicated skills-development centre 
at the Devanahalli Atmanirbhar Complex, adopting 
digitally enabled and flexible production processes, 
and strengthening recruitment for specialised 
talent. Management also emphasised employee 
communication, transport and mobility support as 
facilities, payroll arrangements and work locations 
evolve. These are forward-looking initiatives rather 
than FY2026 outcomes, and their implementation 
will depend on facility commissioning, transaction 
completion, qualified demand and the relevant 
approvals.
10. Outlook
AXISCADES enters FY2027 with a clearer portfolio and a 
favourable demand environment across its priority markets. Global 
aerospace capacity constraints, India’s defence-indigenisation 
drive, accelerated investment in electronics and semiconductors, 
and the opening of the private space ecosystem are expanding 
the opportunity for certified manufacturing, strategic electronics, 
systems integration, AI-led engineering and lifecycle support.
These tailwinds are closely aligned with the capabilities the 
Company is building. The immediate opportunity is to convert 
this favourable market environment into qualified programmes, 
accepted deliveries, cash generation and sustainable returns.
10.1 Market Dynamics and Growth Tailwinds
Aerospace capacity and supply-chain diversification. The global 
aircraft order backlog has exceeded 17,000 aircraft, equivalent 
to nearly 12 years of current production capacity. The mismatch 
between aircraft demand and available production capacity is 
considered unlikely to normalise before 2031–2034. This creates a 
long-duration requirement for additional qualified capacity across 
aerospace tooling, precision and composite manufacturing, 
supply-chain management and component MRO. AXISCADES’ 
engineering pedigree, customer relationships and developing 
manufacturing base provide a relevant platform for moving deeper 
into design-to-build and lifecycle participation. At the same time, 
continuing constraints in engines, specialised materials, electronics 
and skilled talent reinforce the importance of supply-chain 
resilience.Defence modernisation and indigenisation.  India’s 
defence allocation for FY2026-27 increased to `7.85 
lakh crore, including `1.39 lakh crore earmarked 
for procurement from domestic defence industries. 
Approximately 75% of the capital-acquisition budget 
has been reserved for domestic procurement. 
This policy direction supports a growing role for 
capable private-sector participants across strategic 
electronics, missile and radar programmes, land 
systems, unmanned platforms, systems integration 
and complete-system delivery. For AXISCADES, the 
opportunity is to convert its design positions and 
programme relationships into repeat production and 
higher-value integration responsibilities.
Electronics, semiconductors and AI-led 
engineering. India’s semiconductor demand is 
projected to grow at approximately 19% annually 
to around US$90 billion by FY2030. Policy support 
through the India Semiconductor Mission, together with 
the country’s established design talent, is encouraging 
investment across semiconductor design, assembly, 
testing, packaging and system-level integration. These 
trends support the development of ESAI and XiDA 
Inc at the intersection of post-silicon engineering, 
embedded systems, electronics realisation, AI and 
hardware-led solutions.MANAGEMENT DISCUSSION & ANALYSIS

Emergence of India’s private space economy.  IN-SPACe estimates 
that India’s space economy could grow from US$8.4 billion in 2022 to 
US$44 billion by 2033. The Access-to-Space segment, which includes 
satellite manufacturing, launch services and ground infrastructure, is 
projected to expand from US$1.3 billion to US$10.6 billion. This creates 
selective opportunities for AXISCADES in satellite-bus manufacturing, 
payload integration, onboard electronics and computing, cable 
harnesses and space situational awareness. As this remains an 
emerging platform for the Company, investment and capability creation 
will be sequenced through partnerships, qualification milestones and 
identified customer demand.
Importantly, these markets are supported by a shared capability 
foundation. Precision manufacturing, composites, certified assemblies, 
electronics, testing and systems engineering can serve Aerospace, 
Defence and selected Space programmes. This dual- and tri-use 
architecture can support higher asset utilisation, faster capability 
transfer and more efficient capital deployment as programmes scale.
10.2 FY2027 Execution Priorities and Reporting Perimeter
Following the post-year-end Engineering Services divestment 
announcements, the Company’s FY2027 reporting perimeter is 
expected to differ materially from FY2026, subject to transaction 
completion and the applicable accounting treatment. The Company 
has indicated that a quantified update on the revenue transition, 
programme conversion and revised continuing-operations guidance will 
be provided with the Q1 FY2027 investor presentation. Until that update 
is available, forward-looking comparisons remain subject to a bridge 
between the FY2026 reported perimeter and the retained business.
The FY2027 operating agenda is focused on execution. Priorities 
include converting executable orders and year-end carry-forward 
programmes into delivery, inspection, customer acceptance, invoicing 
and collection; strengthening supply-chain resilience; releasing working 
capital; commissioning capacity against qualified demand; completing 
announced transaction milestones; and integrating acquired 
capabilities through disciplined investment and operating frameworks.
Commercial visibility will continue to be presented with clear 
distinctions between firm executable orders, Assured Forecast Visibility, 
L1 or preferred-bidder positions, design and qualification programmes, 
acquisition proposals and the wider opportunity pipeline. Growth in the 
pipeline is encouraging, but operating performance will ultimately be 
determined by the rate and quality of conversion into revenue, margins 
and cash.
10.3 Power 930 Trajectory
Power 930 sets the scale and direction of the Company’s long-term 
value-creation ambition. The strength of the underlying Aerospace, 
Defence, Electronics, AI and Space markets provides a supportive 
demand backdrop. Progress will be demonstrated through tangible 
operating outcomes: programme conversion, timely qualification and 
commissioning, higher capacity utilisation, an improving revenue 
and margin mix, stronger cash conversion, successful acquisition 
integration and growing returns on invested capital.
Subject to transaction completion, the proposed proceeds, together 
with internally generated resources, are expected to create meaningful 
investment capacity. Capital will be deployed progressively, aligned with qualified customer demand, project readiness 
and clearly defined return thresholds. This approach is 
intended to accelerate growth across priority platforms 
while preserving financial resilience and capital 
discipline.
The direction of demand is favourable. The Company’s 
FY2027 focus is to translate that opportunity into 
stronger delivery, cash generation and durable 
shareholder value.

BOARD’S REPORT
STATE OF AFFAIRS / PERFORMANCE REVIEW
During FY26, AXISCADE S delivered a strong operational 
performance, driven by sustained momentum across 
its Aerospace, Defence, Space, and ESAI (Electronics, 
Semiconductors and Artificial Intelligence) businesses. 
Consolidated revenue from operations increased by 12.4% 
year-on-year to `1,159 crore, reflecting robust programme 
execution and continued demand across the Company’s core 
strategic sectors. EBITDA grew by 24.6% to `178 crore, while 
EBITDA margin expanded by approximately 150 basis points to 
15.3%, underscoring the benefits of an enhanced business mix, 
operational leverage, and disciplined execution.
The Company’s core businesses further strengthened their 
contribution to overall performance, with Aerospace, Defence, 
and ESAI activities accounting for approximately 78% of total 
revenue during the year. Growth was supported by increasing 
defence procurement opportunities, the expansion of aerospace 
programmes, strategic investments in electronics, and continued 
enhancement of manufacturing and deep-technology capabilities. 
The Company also progressed several strategic infrastructure 
initiatives and reinforced its position in high-value indigenous 
defence and aerospace programmes.
FY26 was also marked by significant strategic transformation. In 
line with its long-term strategic roadmap, AXISCADES entered 
into definitive agreements for the divestment of its Engineering 
Services business serving the Heavy Engineering, Energy, and 
Automotive sectors. This portfolio realignment is intended to 
sharpen the Company’s focus on high er-growth and higher-margin opportunities in Aerospace Manufacturing, Defence, Space, and 
Deep Technology, while enhancing capital allocation efficiency and 
creating long-term shareholder value.
Reported profitability for the year was impacted by certain 
exceptional and timing-related factors. Revenue recognition 
of approximately `142 crore relating to specific customer 
programmes was deferred to FY27 due to supply chain constraints 
and programme execution timelines. In addition, one-time 
restructuring and transaction-related costs associated with the 
strategic divestment affected reported earnings. Notwithstanding 
these temporary impacts, the underlying performance of the 
business remained robust, with Normalised Profit After Tax 
increasing by 27.6% year-on-year to `83 crore, reflecting the 
strength and resilience of the Company’s operating performance.

VIGIL MECHANISM
The Vigil Mechanism of the Company which also incorporates 
the Whistle blower policy provides a formal mechanism to 
all Directors and employees to approach the Chairman of 
the Audit Committee and make protective disclosures about 
unethical behaviour, actual or suspected fraud or violation 
of the Company’s Code of Conduct or ethics policy. The 
Whistle blower policy is an extension of the Company Code of 
Conduct, which requires every employee to promptly report to 
the Management any actual or possible violation of the Code 
or an event he is aware of, that could affect the business 
or reputation of the Company. The disclosures reported 
are addressed in the manner and within the time frames 
prescribed in the Policy. No personnel of the Company were 
denied access to the Chairman of the Audit Committee. The 
Whistle blower policy which also describes the mechanism 
may be accessed on the Company’s website at

RISK MANAGEMENT POLICY
The Company has formulated and implemented a Risk 
Management Policy which focuses on the identification of 
various elements of risks, if any, which in the opinion of the 
Board, may threaten the existence of the Company.
The Company has a risk identification and management 
framework appropriate to its size and the environment under 
which it operates. The risk management process involves 
identification and periodic assessment of potential risks 
and their impact on the operations, profitability, growth and 
continuity of the business and focuses on risk elements 
pertaining to competitive position in the key market segments, 
business environment, statutory and regulatory changes, 
global economy and business scenario, Currency exchange 
rate fluctuations, resource constraints etc. and initiating timely 
preventive as well as remedial actions.
Reporting and control mechanisms ensure timely information 
availability and facilitates proactive risk management. These 
mechanisms are designed to cascade down to the level of 
line managers so that risk at the transaction level is identified 
and steps are taken towards mitigation in a decentralized 
fashion.
Risks are being continuously monitored in relation to 
business strategy, operations and transactions, statutory/
legal compliance, financial reporting, information technology 
system etc. based on the inputs from both external and 
internal sources like key incidents, Internal audit findings etc.
The Risk Management Committee is responsible for 
monitoring risk levels on various parameters and the senior 
management group ensures implementation of mitigation 
measures, if required. The Audit Committee has additional 
oversight in the area of financial risks and controls.

During the financial year 2025-26, no complaints have

NOMINATION AND REMUNERATION POLICY
INTRODUCTION: 
The Company is a Service Industry and therefore Company’s 
policy strives to consider human resources as its invaluable assets, 
to pay equitable remuneration to all Directors, Key Managerial 
Personnel (KMP) and employees of the Company.
In terms of the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and SEBI 
Listing Regulations as amended from time to time, the Nomination 
and Remuneration Committee has formulated this policy on 
nomination and remuneration of Directors, Key Managerial 
Personnel and Senior Management (if any) and the same is 
approved by the Board of Directors.
OBJECTIVE: 
• To identify persons who are qualified to become Directors 
(Executive, Non Executive and Independent) and persons 
who may be appointed in Senior Management and Key 
Managerial positions, in accordance with the criteria laid 
down 
• Formulating Policy for remuneration for the Directors / KMPs 
and SMPs 
• To specify the manner for effective evaluation of performance 
of Board, its committees and individual Directors as well 
as Key Managerial and Senior Management Personnel and 
review its implementation and compliance. 
• Recommending appointment and removal of Directors, 
KMPs and SMPs to devise a policy on diversity of Board of 
Directors. 
In order to achieve the aforesaid objectives the following policy has 
been originally formulated by the Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee and adopted by the Board of Directors at its meeting 
held on June 23, 2014 with first revision adopted on September 9, 
2014 and second revision adopted on June 27, 2020. 
EFFECTIVE DATE: 
The original policy is effective from April 01, 2014. Any revision to 
the same shall be effective from the date of its adoption by the 
Board.
CONSTITUTION OF THE NOMINATION AND 
REMUNERATION COMMITTEE:
The Board has renamed its Remuneration Committee as 
Nomination and Remuneration Committee on March 27, 2014 and 
reconstituted it on September 9, 2014. 
The NRC shall comprise such Directors as approved by the Board 
of Directors. The Board has the power to reconstitute the NRC in 
conformity with the applicable statutory requirements.APPLICABILITY:
The Policy is applicable to 
• Directors (Executive and Non Executive) 
• Key Managerial Personnel 
• Senior Management Personnel (if any)
GENERAL 
• This Policy is divided in three parts: Part – A covers the 
matters to be dealt with and recommended by the Committee 
to the Board, Part – B covers the appointment and nomination 
and remuneration, PART – C covers proceedings of the 
Committee meetings. 
• The key features of this Company’s policy shall be included in 
the Board’s Report. 
PART – A 
MATTERS TO BE DEALT WITH AND 
RECOMMENDED TO THE BOARD BY 
THE NOMINATION AND REMUNERATION 
COMMITTEE 
The Committee shall: 
• Formulate the criteria for determining qualifications, positive 
attributes and independence of a director. 
• Identify persons who are qualified to become Director and 
persons who may be appointed in Key Managerial and Senior 
Management positions in accordance with the criteria laid 
down. 
• Recommend to the Board, appointment of Director, KMP and 
Senior Management Personnel.
• Performance Evaluation of each Director KMP and Senior 
Management Personnel for the purpose of appraisal or 
removal/ replacement. 
• Policy for Remuneration for Director, KMP and Senior 
Management Personnel. 
• Monitor the Board Diversity and balanced Board 
• Succession planning- recommends to the Board from time 
to time on long term succession plan and also contingency 
plan in case of exigencies, relating to both Board as well as 
Executive management.
• Retirement policy- The retirement age of the directors is fixed 
by the Board of Directors in consultation with the Nomination 
& Remuneration Committee.

PART – B 
POLICY FOR APPOINTMENT AND REMOVAL 
& REMUNERATION OF DIRECTOR, KMP AND 
SENIOR MANAGEMENT 
Policy for appointment and removal & remuneration of Directors, 
KMPs & SMPs:
1. The Committee shall identify and ascertain the qualification, 
expertise, attributes and experience of the person for 
appointment as Director, KMP or at Senior Management 
level and recommend to the Board his / her appointment. 
A person, to be appointed as Director, should possess 
impeccable reputation for integrity, deep expertise and 
insights in sectors / areas relevant to the Company, ability to 
contribute to the Company’s growth and complementary skills 
in relation to the other Board members.
2. For Recommending any person as Executive Director the 
Committee shall take into consideration the provisions of the 
Companies Act, 2013 read together with the Rules prescribed 
there under and Schedule V.
3. For recommending any person as Non Executive Director/ 
Independent Director the Committee shall take into 
consideration the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 read 
together with the Rules prescribed there under and Schedule 
IV along with the criteria for independence defined under SEBI 
Listing Regulation. 
• The Committee shall carry out evaluation of performance 
of Board, its Committees, every Director, KMP and 
Senior Management Personnel at regular interval 
(yearly). 
• Due to reasons for any disqualification mentioned in 
the Companies Act, 2013, rules made there under or 
under any other applicable Act, rules and regulations or 
on the basis of performance evaluation, the Committee 
may recommend, to the Board with reasons recorded 
in writing, removal / replacement of a Director, KMP or 
Senior Management Personnel subject to the provisions 
and compliance of the said Act, rules and regulations. • The Non  Executive / Independent Director may receive 
remuneration by way of fees for attending meetings 
of Board or Committee thereof or commission as per 
Companies Act, 2013. Provided that the amount of such 
sitting fees shall not exceed ` One lakh per meeting 
of the Board or Committee or such amount as may be 
prescribed by the Central Government from time to time. 
Such director may be paid remuneration either by way of 
a monthly payment or at specified percentage of the net 
profits of the company or partly by one way and partly 
by the other. 
• An Independent Director shall not be entitled to any 
stock option of the Company. 
• Remuneration to other employees would be as per 
the company policy as revised from time to time, and 
approved by CEO in consultation with Head HR.
PART – C 
COMMITTEE PROCEEDINGS 
• The Chairman of the Committee will report to the Board (at the 
next Board meeting) on the proceedings of each Committee 
meeting, bringing forward all Committee recommendations 
requiring Board approval. 
• The Secretary will: (a) in conjunction with the Chairman of 
the Committee, settle agendas for and arrange meetings 
of the Committee so as to ensure timely coverage of all the 
Committee’s business; (b) distribute agendas and supporting 
papers to Committee members sufficiently far in advance 
of scheduled meetings to permit adequate preparation; (c) 
keep and distribute minutes of each meeting to Committee 
members; and (d) circulate copies of the minutes to the 
remaining Board members upon request. 
• The Committee shall meet at least once a year. 
• The quorum for a meeting of the Committee will be a majority 
of the members and include at least one Independent 
Director.Annexure – VI

Annexure-VII
ANNUAL REPORT ON CSR ACTIVITIES FOR FINANCIAL YEAR 2025-2026
1. BRIEF OUTLINE ON CSR POLICY OF THE COMPANY:
 The Company recognizes its responsibility as an important stakeholder in the society and strives to work towards the betterment of 
the society constantly. With this objective, and on the recommendation of the CSR Committee, the Board of Directors have approved 
the CSR Policy.
 The CSR activities of the Company mainly focus on the areas of Healthcare, Education, after school life skills and employment 
enhancing skills. The objective is to extend support to the deprived sections like underprivileged kids and differently abled people for 
their economic and social development.
2. COMPOSITION OF CSR COMMITTEE:
 Pursuant to the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Amendment Rules, 2021, the CSR Committee is not required 
to be constituted if amount to be spent by a Company in a year does not exceed ` 50 lakhs. Currently, as the CSR liability for the 
Company is less than `50 lakhs, hence all functions for fulfilling CSR liability shall be carried out by the Board of Directors of the 
Company.
3. Web-link where Composition of CSR committee, CSR Policy and CSR projects approved by the Board are disclosed on the website 
of the company - https://www.axiscades.com/ investor-relations.html
 - CSR Committee of the Company was dissolved in terms of section 135(9) of the Companies Act, 2013 w.e.f. June 11, 2021.
 https://axiscadespdfs.b-cdn.net/CORPORATE%20GOVERNANCE/CORPORATE%20POLICIES/6.pdf
4. Executive summary along with web-link(s) of Impact assessment of CSR projects carried out in pursuance of sub-rule (3) of rule 8 of 
the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Rules, 2014, if applicable.
 Impact assessment is not applicable during the year.
5. (a)  Average net profit of the company as per sub-section (5) of section 135.
  The average net profit / (loss)  for the last three financial years ended is ` 609.15 lakhs hence, applicable.
 (b) Two percent of average net profit of the company as per sub-section (5) section 135 – ` 12,18,000/-
 (c) Surplus arising out of the CSR projects or programmes or activities of the previous financial years – Nil
 (d) Amount required to be set off for the financial year, if any – Nil
 (e) Total CSR obligation for the financial year [(b)+(c)-(d)] – ` 12,18,000/-
6. (a) Amount spent on CSR Projects (both Ongoing Project and other than Ongoing Project): ` 8,14,000/-
 (b) Amount spent in Administrative Overheads: Nil
 (c) Amount spent on Impact Assessment, if applicable, Nil
 (d) Total amount spent for the Financial Year [(a)+(b)+(c)]: ` 8,14,000/-

Governance, leadership and oversight
7. Statement by Director responsible for the business responsibility report, highlighting ESG related challenges, targets 
and achievements (listed entity has flexibility regarding the placement of this disclosure)
 At AXISCADES, sustainability is embedded in our strategy for delivering engineering excellence and creating long-term stakeholder 
value. As a trusted engineering and technology partner to global industries, we believe innovation, operational excellence, and 
responsible business practices must go hand in hand.
 During FY 2025–26, we made significant progress across our ESG priorities. Renewable energy consumption more than doubled, 
reflecting a significant shift towards greater adoption across operations. At the same time, NOx emissions declined from 123 
mg/Nm³ to 49 mg/Nm³, demonstrating the effectiveness of our emission reduction initiatives. We also strengthened our climate 
disclosures by expanding our Scope 3 inventory to include Purchased Goods and Services and Capital Goods, providing a more 
comprehensive view of our value chain emissions.
 Our continued focus on energy efficiency, employee-driven environmental initiatives, and qualitative climate risk assessment 
strengthened our climate governance and contributed to the improvement of our CDP Climate Change score from D to C. Further 
reinforcing our environmental management practices, the Company successfully sustained its ISO 14001:2015 Environmental 
Management System certification during the year.
 Our focus on people continued to deliver positive outcomes, with the overall employee turnover rate reducing by 11.7%, 96% of 
employees receiving skill upgradation training (up from 90%), and participation in human rights training increasing from 36% to 
72%. Beyond our operations, we enhanced engagement with our value chain by conducting dedicated sustainability awareness 
programmes for our business partners, fostering greater alignment on responsible business practices.
 As an engineering solutions provider serving sectors such as aerospace, defence, automotive, energy, and heavy engineering, 
AXISCADES enables customers to develop products and systems that are more energy efficient, resource conscious, and 
technologically advanced. Through our engineering expertise, digital innovation, and responsible business practices, we continue 
to create sustainable value for our stakeholders while contributing to a more resilient future. Going forward, we remain committed to 
strengthening ESG governance, enhancing data transparency, deepening stakeholder engagement, and embedding sustainability 
into every aspect of our engineering excellence.

10. Health and safety management system:
a. Whether an occupational health and safety management system has been implemented by the entity? (Yes/No). If 
yes, the coverage such system?
 Yes, AXISCADES has established a robust Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) management system across all its offices, 
demonstrating its strong commitment to providing a safe and healthy workplace. The Company conducts periodic inspections 
and follows defined protocols to ensure the safety and quality of its facilities, including regular testing of water, food, and indoor 
air quality, monitoring of safety parameters, maintenance of fire extinguishers and smoke detectors, and the conduct of fire-drill 
training sessions. In addition, routine cleaning of air -conditioning ducts is undertaken to maintain optimal indoor air quality, 
reinforcing AXISCADES’ proactive focus on employee well-being and workplace safety.
b. What are the processes used to identify work-related hazards and assess risks on a routine and non-routine basis 
by the entity?
 AXISCADES adopts a structured and proactive approach to hazard identification and risk mitigation across its operations. A 
comprehensive preventive maintenance program is implemented, encompassing quarterly inspections and annual evaluations 
of transformers and electrical panels, along with monthly checks to ensure the operational readiness of fire extinguishers. 
Access to critical areas such as electrical, UPS, and air -conditioning rooms is strictly regulated. In addition, the Company 
carries out regular inspections, internal audits, management reviews, and mock drills as part of its continuous risk monitoring 
framework. All identified hazards are addressed promptly through defined mitigation measures and control mechanisms, 
underscoring AXISCADES’ strong commitment to maintaining a safe and secure workplace.BUSINESS RESPONSIBILITY AND SUSTAINABILITY REPORT  (contd.)

risks. (Y/N)

they observe.

 Yes, the Company has partnered with third-party service providers to offer general medical and healthcare consultations for

about its commitment to values and ethics in business

foundation of Company’s growth. The Company has a 
strong legacy of fair, transparent and ethical governance 
practices. The Company’s primary objective is to create and 
adhere to a corporate culture of fairness and transparency in 
actions of the Management which are the keys to enhancing 
shareholders value and discharge of social responsibility.

i) matters required to be included in the director’s

board’s report in terms of clause (c) of sub-section 
(3) of Section 134 of the Companies Act, 2013;
ii) changes, if any, in accounting policies and 
practices and reasons for the same;

on the exercise of judgment by management;

v) compliance with listing and other legal 
requirements	relating	to	financial	statements;

changes in accounting policies and practices.

of the listed entity with related parties.e. Recommending to the Board the appointment/

any, reported by Auditors.

transactions	(as	defined	by	the	Audit	Committee) 	
submitted by the management.
h.  Scrutiny of inter- corporate loans and investments.
i. Valuation of undertakings or assets of the Company, 
whenever necessary.

NOMINATION AND REMUNERATION POLICY
The Company is in the Service Industry and therefore Company’s 
policies recognizes Human Resource as its true asset and strives 
to pay equitable remuneration to all Directors, Key Managerial 
Personnel (KMP) and employees of the Company.
In terms of the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 and 
Regulation 19 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, the Nomination and 
Remuneration Committee has formulated a policy on nomination 
and remuneration of Directors, Key Managerial Personnel & Senior 
Management and the same is approved by the Board of Directors, 
from time to time.The remuneration considers a balanced blend of Fixed and 
Variable pay, in line with the best market practices, to attract and 
retain talent, to achieve excellence in performance, so as to meet 
its strategic, short-term and long-term goals and objectives of the 
Company.
The Policy sets out the guiding principles for Nomination and 
Remuneration Committee for recommending to the Board, 
remuneration of the Executive Management of the Company.
(i) Policy on Directors’ Remuneration
 The Non-Executive / Independent Directors shall receive 
remuneration by way of sitting fees for attending meetings of 
Board or Committee and Commission as approved by the 
shareholders on September 28, 2023. The amount of such 
fees shall not exceed the limits as may be prescribed by the 
Central Government from time to time.
 The Independent Directors are not entitled to any stock 
options of the Company.
 The Board shall, on the recommendation of the Nomination 
and Remuneration Committee, review and approve the 
remuneration payable to the Non-Executive Directors within 
the overall limits approved by the shareholders.
(ii) Remuneration to Executive Directors and Key 
Managerial Personnel
 The remuneration structure for the Executive Directors and 
Key Managerial Personnel shall consist of:
i) Basic pay
ii)	 Benefits,	Perquisites	and	Allowances
iii) Performance based Variable Pay
iv)	 Retiral	benefits
v) ESOP , as and when granted as per the approved 
Scheme.
 The Board shall, on the recommendation of the Nomination 
and Remuneration Committee, review and approve the 
remuneration payable to the Executive Directors & KMPs’ as 
per applicable statutory regulations and requisite approvals.
(iii) Remuneration to other employees
 The employees shall be evaluated annually based on their 
role,	qualifications,	competencies	and	expertise.	Their

D. RISK MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE
i. The Risk Management Committee of the Company is constituted in line with the provisions of Regulation 21 of SEBI Listing 
Regulations.
ii. The terms of reference of the Risk Management Committee are as under:
(1) To formulate a detailed risk management policy which shall include:
(a)	 A	framework	for	identification	of	internal	and	external	risks	specifically	faced	by	the	listed	entity,	in	particular	including 	
financial,	operational,	sectoral,	sustainability	(particularly,	ESG	related	risks),	information,	cyber	security	risks	or	any	other 	
risk as may be determined by the Committee.
(b)	 Measures	for	risk	mitigation	including	systems	and	processes	for	internal	control	of	identified	risks.
(c) Business continuity plan.
(2) To ensure that appropriate methodology, processes and systems are in place to monitor and evaluate risks associated with the 
business of the Company;
(3) To monitor and oversee implementation of the risk management policy, including evaluating the adequacy of risk management 
systems;
(4) To periodically review the risk management policy, at least once in two years, including by considering the changing industry 
dynamics and evolving complexity;
(5) To keep the Board of Directors informed about the nature and content of its discussions, recommendations and actions to be 
taken;
(6)	 The	appointment,	removal	and	terms	of	remuneration	of	the	Chief	Risk	Officer	(if	any)	shall	be	subject	to	review	by	the	Risk 	
Management Committee.
 The Risk Management Committee shall coordinate its activities with other committees, in instances where there is any overlap 
with activities of such committees, as per the framework laid down by the Board of Directors.
iii. During the FY 2025-2026, two meetings of Risk Management Committee were held on October 14, 2025 and March 30, 2026. The 
necessary quorum was present for each of the meetings.

vii. Share transfer System:
 Pursuant to Regulation 40 of SEBI Listing Regulations (as 
amended), the securities of AXISCADES Technologies Limited 
held in physical mode are not transferable, effective April 01, 
2019. Further in compliance with Securities and Exchange 
Board of India vide circular bearing SEBI/ HO/MIRSD/ REPORT ON CORPORATE GOVERNANCE  (contd.)
MIRSD_PoD/P/CIR/2025/97 dated July 2, 2025, a special 
window is open for re-lodgment of transfer deeds, which were 
lodged prior to the deadline of April 01, 2019 and rejected/ 
returned/	not	attended	to	due	to	deficiency	in	the	documents/ 	
process/ or otherwise , for a period of six months from July 7, 
2025 to January 6, 2026.
 The Securities and Exchange Board of India vide circular 
bearing ref. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2022/8 
dated January 25, 2022, has mandated that, in respect of 
investor services including transmission, duplicate share 
certificate,	transposition,	securities	re-lodged	for	transfer	etc., 	
the listed entity shall issue the securities in dematerialised 
mode only.
 In compliance with the above circular, no securities in physical 
mode are issued by the listed entity.
 The securities, however held in dematerialised mode, are 
freely transferable. The transfer through demat mode takes 
place instantaneously between the transferor, transferee, and 
the Depository Participant through electronic debit/credit of 
the accounts involved.
 KFin Technologies Limited is the common Registrar & Transfer 
Agent for shares held in both physical and dematerialised 
mode. SEBI vide its Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-
PoD-1/P/CIR/2023/37 dated March 16, 2023, considering the enhanced measures to ease dealings in securities market by 
the Investors, has mandated:
a. furnishing of PAN, email address, mobile number, bank 
account details and nomination by holders of physical 
securities,
b. registration of the PAN, Bank details and the nomination 
for dealing with any service request and complaint,
c. linking of PAN and Aadhaar by such date as may be 
specified	by	the	Central	Board	of	Direct	Taxes	to	avoid 	
freezing of folio.
 The prescribed procedure for dealing with the above requests 
have been advised to the shareholders vide our letter dated 
May 29, 2023 and the shareholders are requested to refer 
to the same. In view of the SEBI circular SEBI/HO/ MIRSD/
MIRSD_RTAMB/P/CIR/2022/8 dated January 25, 2022, 
we would like to urge the shareholders holding shares in 
physical form to dematerialize their holdings at the earliest. 
Dematerialised of shares ensures quick, error-free and 
seamless transactions. It is a safe and convenient way 
to trade or invest and enables to monitor portfolio from 
anywhere across the Globe.
	 Confirmation	in	respect	to	the	requests	for	dematerialization 	
of shares is sent to the respective depositories i.e. NSDL and

Assessment of impairment of investment in subsidiaries  (as described in note 2.2(a) and note 5 of the standalone financial 
statements)
As at March 31, 2026, the carrying value of investment in 
subsidiaries in the standalone balance sheet aggregates  
` 41,138.65 lakhs, net of impairment.
The Management assesses annually the existence of impairment 
indicators in respect of its investment in subsidiaries and such 
investments are subject to impairment test.
For the purpose of the above assessment, recoverable amount has 
been determined by forecasting and discounting future cash flows. 
Furthermore, the recoverable amount is based on Management’s 
assumptions of variables and market conditions such as volume 
growth rates, future operating expenditure, discount rates and 
long-term growth rates.
Determination of the recoverable amount of the investment in 
subsidiaries involved judgment due to inherent uncertainty in 
the assumptions supporting the recoverable amount of these 
investments and accordingly, the assessment of impairment of 
investment in subsidiaries were determined to be a key audit 
matter in our audit of the standalone financial statements.Our audit procedures included the following:
• We understood, evaluated and tested Management’s key 
controls over the process of assessment of impairment in 
investments;
• We assessed the Company’s valuation methodology 
applied in determining the recoverable amount. In making 
this assessment, we also assessed the objectivity and 
independence of Company’s specialists involved in the 
process;
• We engaged experts to assess the assumptions around the 
key drivers of the cash flow forecasts including discount 
rates, expected growth rates and long-term growth rates and 
methodologies used by the Management to determine the 
recoverable amount;
• We tested the arithmetical accuracy of the impairment testing 
models; and
• We have assessed the disclosure in the standalone financial 
statements as per the relevant accounting standards.

Key Audit Matters

judgment, were of most significance in our audit of the standalone 
financial statements for the financial year ended March 31, 2026.

Key audit matters How our audit addressed the key audit matter
Revenue Recognition – unbilled revenue  (as described in note 2.2(f), note 7 and note 21 of the standalone financial statements)
Revenue from sale of engineering services for the year ended 
March 31, 2026 amounted to ` 45,466.91 lakhs and unbilled 
receivables as at March 31, 2026 amounted to ` 4,132.07 lakhs.
Revenue from time and material contracts related to engineering 
services are recognised over time as the related services are 
performed, which is pursued based on the efforts spent and 
agreed rate with the customer. Billing is done basis customer 
acceptances. Revenue from the end of last invoicing to the 
reporting date is recognized as unbilled revenue.
Considering significant amount and volume of transactions, there 
is an inherent risk related to the occurrence of unbilled revenue 
at the year-end date. Accordingly, we have determined this area 
to be key audit matters in our audit of the standalone financial 
statements.Our audit procedures included the following:
• We evaluated the Company’s accounting policy for revenue 
recognition and assessed its compliance with Ind AS 115, 
Revenue from Contracts with Customers;
• We assessed the design and tested the operating 
effectiveness of internal controls related to revenue;
• We performed sample test of revenue transactions of unbilled 
revenue at the year-end and traced those to underlying 
terms agreed with customers, proof of service delivery and 
approvals. Also, tested, on a sample basis, invoices raised 
subsequent to year end;
• We assessed aging of unbilled revenue as on the balance 
sheet date and in case of aged items obtained reasons for 
delays and expected timelines for invoicing of the same; and
• Assessed the relevant disclosures in the standalone financial 
statements as per the relevant accounting standards.

Report on the Internal Financial Controls under 
Clause (i) of Sub-section 3 of Section 143 of the 
Companies Act, 2013 (“the Act”)
We have audited the internal financial controls with reference to 
standalone financial statements of AXISCADES Technologies 
Limited (“the Company”) as of March 31, 2026 in conjunction with 
our audit of the standalone financial statements of the Company for 
the year ended on that date.
Management’s Responsibility for Internal 
Financial Controls
The Company’s Management is responsible for establishing 
and maintaining internal financial controls based on the internal 
control over financial reporting criteria established by the Company 
considering the essential components of internal control stated 
in the Guidance Note on Audit of Internal Financial Controls 
Over Financial Reporting issued by the Institute of Chartered 
Accountants of India (“ICAI”). These responsibilities include the 
design, implementation and maintenance of adequate internal 
financial controls that were operating effectively for ensuring the 
orderly and efficient conduct of its business, including adherence 
to the Company’s policies, the safeguarding of its assets, the 
prevention and detection of frauds and errors, the accuracy 
and completeness of the accounting records, and the timely 
preparation of reliable financial information, as required under the 
Companies Act, 2013. 
Auditor’s Responsibility
Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company's 
internal financial controls with reference to these standalone 
financial statements based on our audit. We conducted our audit in 
accordance with the Guidance Note on Audit of Internal Financial 
Controls Over Financial Reporting (the “Guidance Note”) and 
the Standards on Auditing, as specified under section 143(10) of 
the Act, to the extent applicable to an audit of internal financial 
controls, both issued by ICAI. Those Standards and the Guidance Note require that we comply with ethical requirements and plan 
and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about 
whether adequate internal financial controls with reference to these 
standalone financial statements was established and maintained 
and if such controls operated effectively in all material respects.
Our audit involves performing procedures to obtain audit 
evidence about the adequacy of the internal financial controls 
with reference to these standalone financial statements and their 
operating effectiveness. Our audit of internal financial controls with 
reference to standalone financial statements included obtaining an 
understanding of internal financial controls with reference to these 
standalone financial statements, assessing the risk that a material 
weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design and 
operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed 
risk. The procedures selected depend on the auditor’s judgement, 
including the assessment of the risks of material misstatement of 
the financial statements, whether due to fraud or error. 
 We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient 
and appropriate to provide a basis for our audit opinion on the 
Company’s internal financial controls with reference to these 
standalone financial statements.
Meaning of Internal Financial Controls With 
Reference to these Standalone Financial 
Statements
A company's internal financial controls with reference to standalone 
financial statements is a process designed to provide reasonable 
assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and 
the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in 
accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. A 
company's internal financial controls with reference to standalone 
financial statements includes those policies and procedures that 
(1) pertain to the maintenance of records that, in reasonable detail, 
accurately and fairly reflect the transactions and dispositions of 
the assets of the company; (2) provide reasonable assurance ANNEXURE 2
TO THE INDEPENDENT AUDITOR’S REPORT OF EVEN DATE ON THE STANDALONE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS OF 
AXISCADES TECHNOLOGIES LIMITED 
that transactions are recorded as necessary to permit preparation 
of financial statements in accordance with generally accepted 
accounting principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the 
company are being made only in accordance with authorisations 
of management and directors of the company; and (3) provide 
reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely detection 
of unauthorised acquisition, use, or disposition of the company's 
assets that could have a material effect on the financial statements.
Inherent Limitations of Internal Financial 
Controls With Reference to Standalone Financial 
Statements
Because of the inherent limitations of internal financial controls 
with reference to standalone financial statements, including the 
possibility of collusion or improper management override of 
controls, material misstatements due to error or fraud may occur 
and not be detected. Also, projections of any evaluation of the 
internal financial controls with reference to standalone financial 
statements to future periods are subject to the risk that the internal 
financial control with reference to standalone financial statements 
may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or 
that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures may 
deteriorate.Opinion
In our opinion, the Company has, in all material respects, adequate 
internal financial controls with reference to standalone financial 
statements and such internal financial controls with reference 
to standalone financial statements were operating effectively as 
at March 31, 2026, based on the internal control over financial 
reporting criteria established by the Company considering the 
essential components of internal control stated in the Guidance 
Note issued by the ICAI.

1. Corporate information: 
 The Standalone financial statements comprise financial 
statements of AXISCADES Technologies Limited (‘the 
Company’/ ‘AXISCADES’) (CIN: L72200KA1990PLC084435) 
for the year ended March 31, 2026. The Company is a public 
limited company domiciled in India and is incorporated on 
August 24, 1990 under the provisions of the Companies 
Act applicable in India. The Company’s shares are listed for 
trading on the National Stock Exchange of India Limited and 
BSE Limited in India. The registered office of the Company is 
Block C, Second Floor, Kirloskar Business Park, Bengaluru - 
560024, Karnataka, India.
 The Company is principally engaged in the business of 
Technology Services and Solutions. Information on other 
related party relationships of the Company is provided in note 
29.
 The Standalone financial statements were approved for issue 
in accordance with a resolution of the directors on May 27, 
2026.
 The financial statements once approved by the Board of 
directors needs to be adopted by the shareholders at the 
annual general meeting of the company. 
2. Material accounting policies 
2.1 Statement of compliance and basis of preparation
 The Standalone financial statements of the Company have 
been prepared in accordance with Indian Accounting 
Standards (Ind AS) notified under the Companies (Indian 
Accounting Standards) Rules, 2015 (as amended from time to 
time) and presentation requirements of Division II of Schedule 
III to the Companies Act, 2013 (as amended from time to 
time), (Ind AS compliant Schedule III), as applicable to the 
standalone financial statements.
 The standalone financial statements have been prepared on 
a historical cost basis, except for the following assets and 
liabilities which have been measured at fair value:
 Derivative financial instruments,   
 Certain financial assets and liabilities measured at fair value 
(refer accounting policy regarding financial instruments), and 
Contingent consideration arising from business combination
 Equity settled ESOP at grant date fair value
 The accounting policies and related notes further described 
the specific measurements applied for each of the assets and 
liabilities.
 In addition, the carrying values of recognised assets and 
liabilities designated as hedged items in fair value hedges 
that would otherwise be carried at amortised cost are 
adjusted to record changes in the fair values attributable 
to the risks that are being hedged in effective hedge 
relationships. The financial statements are presented in INR and all values 
are rounded to the nearest lakh (INR 00,000), except when 
otherwise indicated.
 The Company has prepared the financial statements on the 
basis that it will continue to operate as a going concern.
2.2 Summary of material accounting policies
a) Investment in subsidiaries and associates
 A subsidiary is an entity that is controlled by another entity.
 An associate is an entity over which the Company has 
significant influence. Significant influence is the power to 
participate in the financial and operating policy decisions 
of the investee but is not control or joint control over those 
policies.
 The Company’s investments in its subsidiaries and associates 
are accounted at cost less impairment.
 Impairment of investments
 The Company reviews its carrying value of investments 
carried at cost annually, or more frequently when there is 
indication for impairment. If the recoverable amount is less 
than its carrying amount, the impairment loss is recorded in 
the Statement of Profit and Loss.
 When an impairment loss subsequently reverses, the carrying 
amount of the Investment is increased to the revised estimate 
of its recoverable amount, so that the increased carrying 
amount does not exceed the cost of the Investment. A 
reversal of an impairment loss is recognised immediately in 
Statement of Profit or Loss.
b) Current versus non-current classification
 The Company segregates assets and liabilities into current 
and non-current categories for presentation in the balance 
sheet after considering its normal operating cycle and 
other criteria set out in Ind AS 1, “Presentation of Financial 
Statements”. For this purpose, current assets and liabilities 
include the current portion of non-current assets and liabilities 
respectively. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are always 
classified as non-current.
 The operating cycle is the time between the acquisition of 
assets for processing and their realization in cash and cash 
equivalents. The Company has identified period up to twelve 
months as its operating cycle.
c) Property, plant and equipment 
 Capital work in progress is stated at cost, net of accumulated 
impairment loss, if any. Plant and equipment are stated at 
cost, net of accumulated depreciation and accumulated 
impairment losses, if any. Such cost includes the cost of 
replacing part of the plant and equipment and borrowing 
costs for long-term construction projects if the recognition 
criteria are met. Repair and maintenance costs are 
recognised in profit or loss as incurred. The present value of (All amounts in ` lakhs, unless otherwise stated)

 Advances paid towards the acquisition of property, plant 
and equipment outstanding at each balance sheet date is 
classified as capital advances under other non-current assets 
and the cost of assets not put to use before such date are 
disclosed under ‘Capital work-in-progress’. Subsequent 
expenditures relating to property, plant and equipment is 
capitalised only when it is probable that future economic 
benefits associated with these will flow to the Company and 
the cost of the item can be measured reliably.
 An item of property, plant and equipment and any significant 
part initially recognised is derecognised upon disposal or 
when no future economic benefits are expected from its 
use or disposal. Any gain or loss arising on derecognition 
of the asset (calculated as the difference between the net 
disposal proceeds and the carrying amount of the asset) is 
included in the statement of profit and loss when the asset is 
derecognised. 
 The Company depreciates property, plant and equipment 
over their estimated useful lives using the straight-line 
method. The estimated useful lives of assets are as follows:
